translations.literal: Yue Zheng, Peng Shi, Shang Lu, Liu Dingzhi
translations.idiomatic: Yue Zheng, Peng Shi, Shang Lu, Liu Dingzhi

sentences.zh: 李賢，字原德，鄧人。

translations.literal: Li Xian, style name Yuande, was a man of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, whose style was Yuande, came from Deng.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試第一，宣德八年成進士。

translations.literal: He ranked first in the provincial examination and in the eighth year of Xuande became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the provincial examinations and passed the jinshi degree in the eighth year of Xuande.

sentences.zh: 奉命察蝗災於河津，授驗封主事，少師楊士奇欲一見，賢竟不往。

translations.literal: Ordered to inspect locust damage at Hejin, he was appointed Registrar of Yifeng; the Junior Preceptor Yang Shiqi wished to meet him once, but Xian in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned to investigate locust plagues at Hejin, he was appointed registrar at Yifeng; Yang Shiqi, the junior preceptor, wished to meet him, but Xian never went.

sentences.zh: 正統初，言：「塞外降人居京師者盈萬，指揮使月俸三十五石，實支僅一石，降人反實支十七石五鬥，是一降人當京官十七員半矣。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengtong he said: "Those who surrendered beyond the frontier and dwell in the capital exceed ten thousand. A commander receives a monthly salary of thirty-five piculs of grain, yet is actually issued only one picul; surrendered men on the contrary are actually issued seventeen piculs and five dou—so that one surrendered man equals seventeen and a half capital officials."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengtong reign he memorialized: "More than ten thousand men who surrendered beyond the frontier now live in the capital. A commander is allotted thirty-five piculs of grain a month but actually receives only one, while a surrendered tribesman actually receives seventeen and a half—so that a single surrendered man costs as much as seventeen and a half metropolitan officials."

sentences.zh: 宜漸出之外，省冗費，且消患未萌。

translations.literal: They ought gradually to be moved outside, saving redundant expense and also extinguishing trouble before it sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: They should gradually be resettled outside the capital to cut waste and to remove a danger before it takes root.

sentences.zh: 」帝不能用。

translations.literal: " The Emperor could not adopt this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor did not act on the proposal.

sentences.zh: 時詔文武臣誥敕，非九年不給。

translations.literal: At that time an edict required that patent letters of appointment for civil and military officials not be granted unless after nine years.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required that civil and military officials receive their patent letters of appointment only after nine years of service.

sentences.zh: 賢言：「限以九年，或官不能滿秩，或親老不待，不得者十八九，無以勸臣下。

translations.literal: Xian said: "Limited to nine years—either an official cannot complete his term, or aged parents cannot wait—and those who fail to obtain them are eight or nine in ten; there is no means to encourage subordinates."
translations.idiomatic: Xian argued: "With a nine-year limit, some officials never complete a full term and others have aged parents who cannot wait; eight or nine out of ten never receive their patents, and there is no way to encourage loyal service."

sentences.zh: 請仍三年便。

translations.literal: Request that the former practice of every three years be restored."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the former rule of every three years be restored."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The Emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷考功郎中，改文選。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Evaluation and then transferred to the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Bureau of Evaluation and then transferred to the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 扈從北征，師覆脫還。

translations.literal: He followed the northern campaign; when the army was destroyed he escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the northern campaign; when the army was annihilated he escaped and made his way back.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年二月上正本十策，曰勤聖學，顧箴警，戒嗜欲，絕玩好，慎舉措，崇節儉，畏天變，勉貴近，振士風，結民心。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Jingtai he submitted ten policies on proper governance: diligent pursuit of sage learning, regard for admonitory maxims, guard against indulgence of desires, cut off fondness for trifles, be careful in conduct, uphold frugality, fear heavenly omens, encourage the noble and near, revive the spirit of the scholar-official, bind the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Jingtai he presented ten fundamental policies: pursue sage learning diligently, heed admonitory maxims, guard against licentious desires, renounce frivolous pleasures, act with care in all matters, uphold frugality, fear heavenly warnings, encourage those of rank who are near the throne, revive the spirit of the scholar-official class, and bind the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，命翰林寫置左右，備省覽。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved them and ordered the Hanlin to copy them and place them at his side for reference.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved them and ordered the Hanlin Academy to copy them and keep them at hand for his review.

sentences.zh: 尋又陳車戰火器之利，帝頗采納。

translations.literal: Soon after he also submitted the advantages of chariot warfare and firearms; the Emperor adopted much of this.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he also argued the advantages of chariot warfare and firearms, and the Emperor adopted much of what he said.

sentences.zh: 是冬，擢兵部右侍郎，轉戶部。

translations.literal: That winter he was promoted to Vice Minister of War, then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was promoted to vice minister of war and then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 也先數貢馬，賢謂輦金帛以強寇自弊，非策。

translations.literal: Esan repeatedly presented tribute horses; Xian said that conveying gold and silks to strengthen a bandit was injuring oneself—this was no strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Esan repeatedly sent tribute horses; Xian said that hauling gold and silks to strengthen a raider was to harm oneself deliberately—not a sound policy.

sentences.zh: 因陳邊備廢馳狀，于謙請下其章厲諸將。

translations.literal: He then set forth the state of frontier defenses fallen into neglect; Yu Qian requested that his memorial be circulated to stiffen the generals.
translations.idiomatic: He then described how frontier defenses had fallen into neglect; Yu Qian asked that his memorial be distributed to rouse the generals.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部，采古二十二君行事可法者。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, he collected conduct of twenty-two ancient rulers that could serve as models.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, he gathered the conduct of twenty-two ancient rulers that could serve as models.

sentences.zh: 曰《鑒古錄》，上之。

translations.literal: He called it 《Records for Mirroring Antiquity》 and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He titled it 《Records for Mirroring Antiquity》 and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，命兼翰林學士，入直文淵閣，與徐有貞同預機務。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored, [Xian] was ordered concurrently to serve as Hanlin Academician, enter the Wenyuan Pavilion for confidential duty, and share in affairs of state with Xu Youzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, Xian was appointed concurrently as Hanlin academician, entered the Wenyuan Pavilion on confidential duty, and shared state affairs with Xu Youzhen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 賢氣度端凝，奏對皆中機宜，帝深眷之。

translations.literal: Xian's bearing was dignified and composed; in audience his replies always hit what mattered, and the Emperor deeply favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's bearing was dignified and steady; in audience his answers always struck the right point, and the Emperor held him in deep regard.

sentences.zh: 山東饑，發帑振不足，召有貞及賢議，有貞謂頒振多中飽。

translations.literal: Shandong suffered famine; funds were released for relief but proved insufficient; [the Emperor] summoned Youzhen and Xian to discuss. Youzhen said that distributing relief was largely siphoned off in transit.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong suffered famine, treasury funds released for relief proved insufficient; the Emperor summoned Youzhen and Xian to discuss the matter. Youzhen said that relief distributions were largely embezzled in transit.

sentences.zh: 賢曰：「慮中飽而不貸，坐視民死，是因噎廢食也。

translations.literal: Xian said: "Fearing embezzlement in transit and therefore not lending relief is to watch the people die of hunger because one choked—abandoning food for fear of choking."
translations.idiomatic: Xian said: "To fear embezzlement and withhold relief, watching the people starve, is to give up eating for fear of choking."

sentences.zh: 」遂命增銀。

translations.literal: " [The Emperor] then ordered increased silver [for relief].
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then ordered additional silver for relief.

sentences.zh: 石亨、曹吉祥與有貞爭權，並忌賢。

translations.literal: Shi Heng and Cao Jixiang struggled for power with Youzhen and alike resented Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng and Cao Jixiang were locked in a power struggle with Youzhen and equally resented Xian.

sentences.zh: 諸御史論亨、吉祥，亨、吉祥疑出有貞、賢意，訴之帝，下二人獄。

translations.literal: Various censors impeached Heng and Jixiang; Heng and Jixiang suspected this issued from Youzhen and Xian, accused them to the Emperor, and the two men were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When censors impeached Heng and Jixiang, the two men suspected Youzhen and Xian were behind it; they accused them to the Emperor, and both men were thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 會有風雷變，得釋，謫賢福建參政。

translations.literal: When wind and thunder changed [as an omen] they were released; Xian was demoted to Assistant Administrator of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: When wind and thunder shifted as an omen they were released; Xian was demoted to assistant administrator of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 未行，王翺奏賢可大用，遂留為吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Before he set out, Wang Ao memorialized that Xian could be greatly used; he was therefore kept as Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, Wang Ao memorialized that Xian merited greater use; he was kept on as left vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 逾月，復尚書，直內閣如故。

translations.literal: A month later he was again Minister and attended the inner cabinet as before.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was restored as minister and resumed his seat in the inner cabinet as before.

sentences.zh: 亨知帝向賢，怒，然無可如何，乃佯與交歡。

translations.literal: Heng knew the Emperor leaned toward Xian and was angry, yet could do nothing; he therefore feigned friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Heng knew the Emperor favored Xian and was furious, yet could do nothing about it; he therefore pretended friendship.

sentences.zh: 賢亦深自匿，非宣召不入，而帝益親賢，顧問無虛日。

translations.literal: Xian also deeply kept himself concealed—unless summoned by imperial announcement he did not enter—and the Emperor grew all the closer to Xian, consulting him without idle days.
translations.idiomatic: Xian also kept himself deeply withdrawn, entering court only when summoned by imperial announcement; yet the Emperor drew still closer to him and consulted him without a day's lapse.

sentences.zh: 孛來近塞獵。

translations.literal: Bolai approached the frontier to hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Bolai came near the frontier to hunt.

sentences.zh: 亨言傳國璽在彼，可掩而取，帝色動。

translations.literal: Heng said the dynastic seal was with him and could be seized by ambush; the Emperor's expression stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Heng said the imperial seal was with Bolai and could be taken in a surprise attack; the Emperor's expression changed.

sentences.zh: 賢言釁不可啟，璽不足寶，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Xian said that provocation must not be started and the seal was no treasure worth coveting; the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said that provocation must not be invited and the seal was no treasure worth the risk; the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 亨益惡賢。

translations.literal: Heng hated Xian all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Heng hated Xian all the more.

sentences.zh: 時帝亦厭亨、吉祥驕橫，屏人語賢曰：「此輩幹政，四方奏事者先至其門，為之奈何？

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor also wearied of Heng and Jixiang's arrogance; dismissing attendants he said to Xian: "These men interfere in government; memorialists from the four quarters reach their gates first—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had also grown weary of Heng and Jixiang's arrogance; dismissing his attendants he said to Xian: "These men meddle in government affairs; memorials from every quarter reach their gates before mine. What can be done?"

sentences.zh: 」賢曰：「陛下惟獨斷，則趨附自息。

translations.literal: " Xian said: "If Your Majesty alone decides, those who rush to court them will cease of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: " Xian said: "If Your Majesty decides every matter on your own authority, the rush to court them will die away of itself."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「向嘗不用其言，乃怫然見辭色。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Once when their advice was not used they showed displeasure and took leave with angry faces."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Once when I did not follow their advice they showed displeasure and took their leave with angry faces."

sentences.zh: 」賢曰：「願制之以漸。

translations.literal: " Xian said: "I hope Your Majesty will restrain them gradually."
translations.idiomatic: " Xian said: "I hope Your Majesty will restrain them step by step."

sentences.zh: 」當亨、吉祥用事，賢顧忌不敢盡言，然每從容論對，所以裁抑之者甚至。

translations.literal: While Heng and Jixiang held power Xian, out of caution, did not dare speak fully; yet whenever he answered at ease his restraints on them were very strong.
translations.idiomatic: While Heng and Jixiang held power, Xian, out of caution, did not dare speak his whole mind; yet whenever he answered at ease, the restraints he placed on them were very strong indeed.

sentences.zh: 及亨得罪，帝復問賢「奪門」事。

translations.literal: When Heng was punished the Emperor again asked Xian about the "Seizing the Gate" affair.
translations.idiomatic: After Heng was punished, the Emperor again asked Xian about the "Seizing the Gate" coup.

sentences.zh: 賢曰：「『迎駕』則可，『奪門』豈可示後？

translations.literal: Xian said: "'Welcoming the Imperial Carriage' was permissible; 'Seizing the Gate'—how could that be shown to posterity?"
translations.idiomatic: Xian said: "'Welcoming the imperial carriage' was permissible, but how could 'Seizing the Gate' be held up as an example to posterity?"

sentences.zh: 天位乃陛下固有，『奪』即非順。

translations.literal: The throne was inherently Your Majesty's; to 'seize' it was not in accord with the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was inherently yours, Your Majesty; to 'seize' it was not in accord with right order.

sentences.zh: 且爾時幸而成功，萬一事機先露，亨等不足惜，不審置陛下何地！

translations.literal: Moreover, had it fortunately succeeded then, yet if the plan had been exposed first—Heng and the rest were not worth pity, but where would Your Majesty have been placed!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, even if it had fortunately succeeded, had the plot been exposed beforehand—Heng and the rest would not be worth pity, but where would that have left Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 」帝悟曰：「然。

translations.literal: " The Emperor understood and said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor understood and said: "You are right."

sentences.zh: 」賢曰：「若郕王果不起，群臣表請陛下復位，安用擾攘為？

translations.literal: " Xian said: "Had the Prince of Cheng in fact not risen, the officials in a body would have memorialized begging Your Majesty's restoration—why need turmoil?"
translations.idiomatic: " Xian said: "If the Prince of Cheng had in fact not recovered, the officials would have memorialized as a body begging Your Majesty's restoration—why need all that turmoil?"

sentences.zh: 此輩又安所得邀升賞，招權納賄安自起？

translations.literal: These men moreover would not have won promotions and rewards—whence would they have drawn power and taken bribes?"
translations.idiomatic: These men moreover would never have won promotions and rewards—whence would they have drawn power and taken bribes?

sentences.zh: 老成耆舊依然在職，何至有殺戮降黜之事致幹天象？

translations.literal: The old and experienced would still have remained in office—how could there have been killings, demotions, and dismissals provoking heavenly signs?"
translations.idiomatic: The seasoned elders would still have held office—how could there have been killings, demotions, and dismissals that provoked heavenly signs?"

sentences.zh: 《易》曰『開國承家，小人勿用』，正謂此也。

translations.literal: The 《Changes》 says 'In founding a state and continuing the family, do not employ petty men'—it speaks precisely of this."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Book of Changes》 says, 'In founding a state and handing on the family, do not employ petty men'—it speaks precisely of this."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "You are right."

sentences.zh: 」詔自今章奏勿用「奪門」字，並議革冒功者四千余人。

translations.literal: An edict from then on forbade the words "Seizing the Gate" in memorials, and together they discussed stripping false merit from more than four thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade the phrase "Seizing the Gate" in memorials from that day forward, and they discussed stripping false merit from more than four thousand men.

sentences.zh: 至成化初，諸被革者訴請。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Chenghua those stripped submitted appeals.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chenghua reign those who had been stripped appealed for restoration.

sentences.zh: 復以賢言，並奪太平侯張瑾、興濟伯楊宗爵，時論益大快之。

translations.literal: On Xian's advice again, the Peace Marquis Zhang Jin and the Baron of Promoting Relief Yang Zong were also stripped of their ranks; public opinion was all the more delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Again on Xian's advice, the Peace Marquis Zhang Jin and the Baron of Promoting Relief Yang Zong were also stripped of their titles, to the even greater satisfaction of public opinion.

sentences.zh: 帝既任賢，所言皆見聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor having entrusted affairs to Xian, what he said was all followed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Emperor had entrusted affairs to Xian, his counsel was followed in every matter.

sentences.zh: 于謙嘗分遣降人南征，陳汝言希宦官指，盡召之還。

translations.literal: Yu Qian had once dispatched surrendered men south on campaign; Chen Ruyan, courting the eunuchs' wishes, recalled them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian had once dispatched surrendered tribesmen south on campaign; Chen Ruyan, courting the eunuchs' wishes, recalled them all.

sentences.zh: 賢力言不可。

translations.literal: Xian strongly said this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Xian argued forcefully that this must not be done.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾亦悔之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I too regret it."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "I regret it as well."

sentences.zh: 今已就道，後當聽其願去者。

translations.literal: "They are already on the road; hereafter let those who wish to leave do so."
translations.idiomatic: "They are already on the march; hereafter let those who wish to leave do so."

sentences.zh: 」帝憂軍官支俸多，歲入不給。

translations.literal: The Emperor worried that military officers' salaries were many and annual revenue could not cover them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor worried that military officers' salaries were too numerous and annual revenue could not cover them.

sentences.zh: 賢請汰老弱於外，則費省而人不覺。

translations.literal: Xian requested that the aged and weak be eliminated outside [the capital]—expense would be saved and the men would not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Xian asked that the aged and weak be weeded out in the provinces; expense would be saved and no one would notice.

sentences.zh: 帝深納焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor adopted the proposal wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 時歲有邊警，天下大水，江南北尤甚。

translations.literal: At that time there were frontier alarms every year and great floods throughout the empire, especially south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: In those years frontier alarms came every year and great floods struck the empire, especially south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 賢外籌邊計，內請寬百姓，罷一切征求。

translations.literal: Xian outwardly planned frontier strategy and inwardly asked leniency for the people and cessation of all exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Xian planned frontier strategy; inwardly he asked leniency for the people and an end to every exaction.

sentences.zh: 帝用其言，四方得蘇息。

translations.literal: The Emperor used his words and the four quarters obtained respite.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor followed his counsel and the realm obtained respite.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，空中有聲，帝欲禳之，命賢撰青詞。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year a sound appeared in the sky; the Emperor wished to offer ritual expiation and ordered Xian to draft a green prayer.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year a sound was heard in the sky; the Emperor wished to perform expiatory rites and ordered Xian to draft a green prayer.

sentences.zh: 賢言君不恤民，天下怨叛，厥有鼓妖。

translations.literal: Xian said that when a ruler does not care for the people the realm resents and rebels—that is why there are drum demons [an omen].
translations.idiomatic: Xian said that when a ruler does not care for his people the realm resents and rebels—and that is why there are drum demons in the sky.

sentences.zh: 因請行寬恤之政，又請罷江南織造，清錦衣獄，止邊臣貢獻，停內外采買。

translations.literal: He therefore asked to carry out policies of leniency, also asked to stop Jiangnan weaving, clear the Jinyi prison, halt border officials' tribute presents, and stop inner and outer purchases.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore asked for policies of leniency, also to halt Jiangnan weaving, clear the Jinyi prison, stop tribute from frontier officials, and end purchases inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 帝難之。

translations.literal: The Emperor found it hard.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor found it difficult to accept.

sentences.zh: 賢執爭數四，同列皆懼。

translations.literal: Xian argued repeatedly several times; his colleagues were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Xian argued repeatedly on four points; his colleagues were all afraid.

sentences.zh: 賢退曰：「大臣當知無不言，可卷舌偷位耶？

translations.literal: Xian on withdrawing said: "A great minister should know there is nothing he may not say—can one roll up one's tongue and steal one's position?"
translations.idiomatic: On withdrawing, Xian said: "A great minister should know there is nothing he may not say—can one bite one's tongue and cling to office?"

sentences.zh: 」終天順之世，賢為首輔，呂原、彭時佐之，然賢委任最專。

translations.literal: Throughout the Tianshun reign Xian was chief minister, with Lu Yuan and Peng Shi assisting, yet Xian's commission was most exclusive.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Tianshun reign Xian was chief minister, assisted by Lu Yuan and Peng Shi, yet Xian's commission was the most exclusive.

sentences.zh: 初，御史劉濬劾柳溥敗軍罪，觸帝怒。

translations.literal: At first Censor Liu Jun impeached Liu Pu for defeat in battle and provoked the Emperor's anger.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Censor Liu Jun impeached Liu Pu for defeat in battle and provoked the Emperor's anger.

sentences.zh: 賢言御史耳目官，不宜譴。

translations.literal: Xian said that censors are the organs of hearing and sight and ought not to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said that censors are the emperor's eyes and ears and ought not to be punished.

sentences.zh: 石亨譖賢曲護。

translations.literal: Shi Heng slandered Xian for partial protection.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng slandered Xian for shielding the censor unfairly.

sentences.zh: 帝浸疏賢，尋悟，待之如初。

translations.literal: The Emperor gradually grew distant from Xian, but soon understood and treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor gradually grew cool toward Xian, but soon understood and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 每獨對，良久方出。

translations.literal: Whenever alone in audience he was long before emerging.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was received in private audience, he remained a long while before emerging.

sentences.zh: 遇事必召問可否，或遣中官就問。

translations.literal: When affairs arose he was sure to be summoned to ask whether [a course] was feasible, or palace eunuchs were sent to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs arose the Emperor was sure to summon him to ask whether a course was feasible, or sent palace eunuchs to inquire.

sentences.zh: 賢務持大體，尤以惜人才、開言路為急。

translations.literal: Xian strove to hold to the larger pattern, especially urgent to cherish talent and open the avenue of speech.
translations.idiomatic: Xian strove to uphold the larger pattern of governance, especially urgent to cherish talent and open the avenue of frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 所薦引年富、軒輗、耿九疇、王竑、李秉、程信、姚夔、崔恭、李紹等，皆為名臣。

translations.literal: Those he recommended—Nian Fu, Xuan Yuan, Geng Jiuchou, Wang Hong, Li Bing, Cheng Xin, Yao Kui, Cui Gong, Li Shao, and others—were all renowned ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Those he recommended—Nian Fu, Xuan Yuan, Geng Jiuchou, Wang Hong, Li Bing, Cheng Xin, Yao Kui, Cui Gong, Li Shao, and others—were all renowned ministers.

sentences.zh: 時勸帝延見大臣，有所薦，必先與吏、兵二部論定之。

translations.literal: He often urged the Emperor to extend audience to great ministers; whatever he wished to recommend he first discussed and settled with the Ministries of Personnel and War.
translations.idiomatic: He often urged the Emperor to receive great ministers in audience; whatever he wished to recommend he first discussed and settled with the ministries of personnel and war.

sentences.zh: 及入對，帝訪文臣，請問王翺；

translations.literal: When entering audience, if the Emperor inquired about civil officials he asked about Wang Ao;
translations.idiomatic: When he entered audience, if the Emperor inquired about civil officials, Xian would ask about Wang Ao;

sentences.zh: 武臣，請問馬昂。

translations.literal: for military officials he asked about Ma Ang.
translations.idiomatic: for military officials, about Ma Ang.

sentences.zh: 兩人相左右，故言無不行，而人不病其專，惟群小與為難。

translations.literal: The two men supported each other from either side, so his words were all followed yet men did not resent his monopoly—only petty men found him hard to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: The two men supported him from either side, so his counsel was always followed yet men did not resent his monopoly—only petty men made trouble for him.

sentences.zh: 曹欽之反也，擊賢東朝房，執將殺之，逼草奏釋己罪。

translations.literal: When Cao Qin's rebellion broke out, [rebels] struck Xian's eastern audience chamber, seized him intending to kill him, and forced him to draft a memorial releasing their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Qin rebelled, rebels struck Xian's eastern audience chamber, seized him intending to kill him, and forced him to draft a memorial absolving their crimes.

sentences.zh: 賴王翺救，乃免。

translations.literal: Thanks to Wang Ao's rescue he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Wang Ao's rescue he was spared.

sentences.zh: 賢密疏請擒賊黨。

translations.literal: Xian secretly memorialized asking to arrest the rebel clique.
translations.idiomatic: Xian secretly memorialized asking that the rebel clique be arrested.

sentences.zh: 時方擾攘，不知賢所在。

translations.literal: At the time turmoil was just beginning and they did not know where Xian was.
translations.idiomatic: At the time turmoil had just broken out and no one knew where Xian was.

sentences.zh: 得疏，帝大喜。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived the Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived the Emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 裹傷入見，慰勞之，特加太子太保。

translations.literal: Binding his wounds he entered audience; [the Emperor] comforted him and specially added Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Binding his wounds he entered audience; the Emperor comforted him and specially added the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 賢因言，賊既誅，急宜詔天下停不急務，而求直言以通閉塞。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon said that once the rebels were executed they should urgently proclaim throughout the realm a halt to non-urgent affairs and seek straight counsel to open what was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Xian then said that once the rebels were executed the court should urgently proclaim throughout the realm a halt to non-urgent affairs and seek frank counsel to open what had been blocked.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 門達方用事，錦衣官校恣橫為劇患。

translations.literal: Men Da was then in power and Jinyi surveillance officers ran rampant as a severe scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Men Da was then in power, and Jinyi surveillance officers ran rampant as a severe scourge.

sentences.zh: 賢累請禁止，帝召達誡諭之。

translations.literal: Xian repeatedly asked to forbid this; the Emperor summoned Da and admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian repeatedly asked that this be forbidden; the Emperor summoned Da and admonished him.

sentences.zh: 達怙寵益驕，賢乘間復具陳達罪，帝復召戒達。

translations.literal: Da, relying on favor, grew all the more arrogant; Xian seized an opening and again fully set forth Da's crimes, and the Emperor again summoned and warned Da.
translations.idiomatic: Da, relying on imperial favor, grew all the more arrogant; Xian seized an opening and again set forth Da's crimes in full, and the Emperor again summoned and warned him.

sentences.zh: 達銜次骨，因袁彬獄陷賢，賢幾不免，語載達傳。

translations.literal: Da bore a grudge to the bone; through Yuan Bin's prison case he trapped Xian, and Xian nearly perished—the account is in Da's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Da bore a lasting grudge; through the Yuan Bin prison case he trapped Xian, and Xian nearly perished—the full account appears in Da's biography.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，臥文華殿。

translations.literal: The Emperor was unwell and lay in the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fell ill and lay in the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 會有間東宮於帝者，帝頗惑之，密告賢。

translations.literal: Someone slandered the Eastern Palace to the Emperor; the Emperor was quite confused and secretly told Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered the crown prince to the Emperor; the Emperor was deeply troubled and confided in Xian in secret.

sentences.zh: 賢頓首伏地曰：「此大事，願陛下三思。

translations.literal: Xian kowtowed prostrate and said: "This is a great matter; I hope Your Majesty will think thrice."
translations.idiomatic: Xian kowtowed and said prostrate on the ground: "This is a grave matter; I beg Your Majesty to think it over three times."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然則必傳位太子乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Then must the throne be passed to the Crown Prince?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Then must the throne be passed to the crown prince?"

sentences.zh: 」賢又頓首曰：「宗社幸甚。

translations.literal: Xian again kowtowed and said: "Fortunate indeed for the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Xian kowtowed again and said: "Fortunate indeed for the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 」帝起，立召太子至。

translations.literal: The Emperor rose and immediately summoned the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rose and immediately summoned the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 賢扶太子令謝。

translations.literal: Xian supported the Crown Prince and made him give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Xian supported the crown prince and had him give thanks.

sentences.zh: 太子謝，抱帝足泣，帝亦泣，讒竟不行。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince gave thanks, embraced the Emperor's feet and wept; the Emperor too wept, and the slander in the end did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince gave thanks, embraced the Emperor's feet, and wept; the Emperor wept as well, and the slander in the end did not prevail.

sentences.zh: 門達既竄，其黨多投匿名書構賢。

translations.literal: After Men Da fled, his faction mostly sent anonymous letters framing Xian.
translations.idiomatic: After Men Da fled, most of his faction sent anonymous letters to frame Xian.

sentences.zh: 賢乞罷，有詔慰留。

translations.literal: Xian begged to retire; an edict comforted him and kept him on.
translations.idiomatic: Xian asked to resign; an edict comforted him and kept him at his post.

sentences.zh: 吳後廢，言官請誅牛玉，語侵賢，又有造蜚語構賢者。

translations.literal: After the deposed Wu empress, remonstrating officials asked that Niu Yu be executed—words that implicated Xian—and there were also those who manufactured slander to frame Xian.
translations.idiomatic: After the deposed Empress Wu, remonstrating officials called for Niu Yu's execution in language that implicated Xian, and others manufactured slander to frame him.

sentences.zh: 帝命衛士宿賢家，護出入。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered guards to lodge at Xian's home to protect his comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered guards to lodge at Xian's home to protect him when he went out or returned.

sentences.zh: 成化二年三月遭父喪，詔起復。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Chenghua he suffered his father's death; an edict ordered him recalled from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Chenghua he suffered his father's death; an edict ordered him recalled from mourning service.

sentences.zh: 三辭不許，遣中官護行營葬。

translations.literal: He thrice declined but was not permitted; palace eunuchs were sent to escort him and arrange the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He declined three times but was not permitted; palace eunuchs were sent to escort him and oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 還至京，又辭。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital he again declined.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital he declined again.

sentences.zh: 遣使宣意，遂視事。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to announce the imperial intent, and he then took up office.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent to convey the imperial intent, and he then resumed his duties.

sentences.zh: 其年冬卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: That winter he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he died, aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝震悼，贈太師，謚文達。

translations.literal: The Emperor was shaken with grief, posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, posthumous name Wendate.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was shaken with grief, posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor, and gave him the posthumous name Wendate.

sentences.zh: 賢自以受知人主，所言無不盡。

translations.literal: Xian deemed that having won his sovereign's trust, there was nothing he did not say fully.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xian felt he had won his sovereign's trust, there was nothing he held back in counsel.

sentences.zh: 景帝崩，將以汪後殉葬，用賢言而止。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingdi died, they were about to bury the Wang empress as a companion sacrifice; on Xian's words this was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingdi died, the court was about to bury Empress Wang as a companion sacrifice; on Xian's advice this was stopped.

sentences.zh: 惠帝少子幽禁已六十年，英宗憐欲赦之，以問賢。

translations.literal: The deposed young son of Emperor Hui had been confined for sixty years; Emperor Yingzong pitied him and wished to pardon him, and asked Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed young son of Emperor Hui had been confined for sixty years; Emperor Yingzong pitied him and wished to pardon him, and asked Xian.

sentences.zh: 賢頓首曰：「此堯、舜用心也！

translations.literal: Xian kowtowed and said: "This is the mind of Yao and Shun!"
translations.idiomatic: Xian kowtowed and said: "This is the mind of Yao and Shun!"

sentences.zh: 天地祖宗實式憑之。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth and the imperial ancestors surely rely on this.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth and the imperial ancestors surely rely on this.

sentences.zh: 」帝意乃決。

translations.literal: The Emperor's intent was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's mind was then made up.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗祭山川壇，以夜出未便，欲遣官代祀。

translations.literal: The Emperor once sacrificed at the mountain and river altar; going out at night was inconvenient, and he wished to send an official to substitute.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once sacrificed at the mountain and river altar; going out at night was inconvenient, and he wished to send an official to substitute for him.

sentences.zh: 賢引祖訓爭之，卒成禮而還。

translations.literal: Xian cited ancestral instruction and argued; in the end the rite was completed and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xian cited ancestral instruction and argued against it; in the end the rite was completed and he returned.

sentences.zh: 嘗言內帑余財，不以恤荒濟軍，則人主必生侈心，而移之於土木禱祠聲色之用。

translations.literal: He once said that surplus wealth in the inner treasury, if not used to relieve famine and support the army, would make the ruler grow extravagant and shift it to use in earthworks, prayers, and the pleasures of sound and color.
translations.idiomatic: He once said that surplus wealth in the inner treasury, if not used to relieve famine and support the army, would make the ruler grow extravagant and shift it to earthworks, prayers, and the pleasures of sound and color.

sentences.zh: 前後頻請發帑振貸恤邊，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Before and after he repeatedly asked to open the treasury for relief and loans to comfort the frontier—beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he asked to open the treasury for relief, loans, and frontier support—too many times to count.

sentences.zh: 故事，方面官敕三品京官保舉。

translations.literal: By precedent, provincial officials' patents were guaranteed by capital officials of third rank.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, patents for provincial officials required guarantee by capital officials of third rank.

sentences.zh: 賢患其營競，令吏部每缺舉二人，請帝簡用。

translations.literal: Xian worried about their competition for patronage and ordered the Ministry of Personnel each vacancy to nominate two men, asking the Emperor to choose.
translations.idiomatic: Xian worried about their competition for patronage and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to nominate two men for each vacancy, asking the Emperor to choose.

sentences.zh: 並推之例始此。

translations.literal: The precedent of nomination and promotion together began here.
translations.idiomatic: The precedent of joint nomination and promotion began here.

sentences.zh: 自三楊以來，得君無如賢者。

translations.literal: Since the Three Yangs, no one had won the ruler's trust like Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Three Yangs, no one had won the ruler's trust as Xian did.

sentences.zh: 然自郎署結知景帝，超擢侍郎，而所著書顧謂景帝為荒淫。

translations.literal: Yet from his beginning as a director when he won Jingdi's trust and was abruptly promoted to vice minister, in his writings he nevertheless called Emperor Jing dissolute and profligate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from his start in the secretariat, when he won Jingdi's trust and was abruptly promoted to vice minister, in his writings he nevertheless called Emperor Jing dissolute and profligate.

sentences.zh: 其抑葉盛，擠嶽正，不救羅倫，尤為世所惜雲。

translations.literal: His suppressing Ye Sheng, squeezing out Yue Zheng, and not saving Luo Lun were especially regretted by the world.
translations.idiomatic: His suppressing Ye Sheng, squeezing out Yue Zheng, and not saving Luo Lun were especially regretted by the world.

sentences.zh: 呂原，字逢原，秀水人。

translations.literal: Lu Yuan, style name Fengyuan, was a man of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuan, whose style was Fengyuan, came from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 父嗣芳，萬泉教諭。

translations.literal: His father Sifang was instructor at Wanquan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sifang was instructor at Wanquan.

sentences.zh: 兄本，景州訓導。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ben was instructor at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ben was instructor at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 嗣芳老，就養景州，與本相繼卒。

translations.literal: Sifang aged and went to Jingzhou for support; he and Ben died one after another.
translations.idiomatic: When Sifang grew old he went to Jingzhou for support; he and Ben died one after another.

sentences.zh: 貧不能歸葬，厝於景，原時至墓慟哭。

translations.literal: Too poor to return them for burial, they were stored at Jing; Yuan would go to the tomb and weep bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to return them for burial, they were stored at Jing; Yuan would go to the tomb and weep bitterly.

sentences.zh: 久之，奉母南歸，家益貧。

translations.literal: After long while he escorted his mother south to return home; the family grew still poorer.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he escorted his mother south to return home; the family grew still poorer.

sentences.zh: 知府黃懋奇原文，補諸生，遣入學，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: Prefect Huang Maoqi admired his writing, made him a licensed student, sent him to school, and he ranked first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Huang Maoqi admired his writing, made him a licensed student, sent him to the academy, and he ranked first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 正統七年，進士及第，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhengtong he passed the jinshi examination with highest honors and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhengtong he passed the jinshi examination with highest honors and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 十二年，與侍講裴綸等十人同選入東閣肄業，直經筵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he and Lecturer Pei Lun and ten others were jointly selected to study in the Eastern Pavilion and attend the classic lecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he and Lecturer Pei Lun and ten others were jointly selected to study in the Eastern Pavilion and attend the classic lecture.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，進侍講，與同官倪謙授小內侍書於文華殿東廡。

translations.literal: Early in Jingtai he was promoted to Lecturer and with his colleague Ni Qian taught the young palace attendants writing in the eastern veranda of Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingtai he was promoted to lecturer and, with his colleague Ni Qian, taught the young palace attendants writing in the eastern veranda of the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝至，命謙講《國風》。

translations.literal: When the Emperor came he ordered Qian to lecture on the Odes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor came he ordered Qian to lecture on the Odes.

sentences.zh: 原講《堯典》，皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Yuan lectured on the Canon of Yao—all pleased the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan lectured on the Canon of Yao—both pleased the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 問何官，並以中允兼侍講對。

translations.literal: Asked what office they held, both answered as Junior Tutors concurrently serving as Lecturers.
translations.idiomatic: Asked what offices they held, both answered that they were junior tutors concurrently serving as lecturers.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「品同耳，何相兼為？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The ranks are the same—why hold both offices?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The ranks are the same—why hold both offices at once?"

sentences.zh: 」進二人侍講學士，兼中允。

translations.literal: Both were promoted Lecturer-Academicians, concurrently Junior Tutors.
translations.idiomatic: Both were promoted to lecturer-academicians, concurrently junior tutors.

sentences.zh: 尋進左春坊大學士。

translations.literal: Soon promoted Grand Secretary of the Left Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to grand secretary of the left Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 天順初，改通政司右參議，兼侍講。

translations.literal: Early in Tianshun he was changed to Right Assistant Administrator of the Communications Office, concurrently Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianshun he was transferred to right assistant administrator of the Communications Office, concurrently lecturer.

sentences.zh: 徐有貞、李賢下獄之明日，命入內閣預機務。

translations.literal: The day after Xu Youzhen and Li Xian were imprisoned he was ordered into the inner cabinet to share in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Xu Youzhen and Li Xian were imprisoned he was ordered into the inner cabinet to share in confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 石享、曹吉祥用事，貴倨，獨敬原。

translations.literal: Shi Heng and Cao Jixiang held power, arrogant as nobles; only toward Yuan they showed respect.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng and Cao Jixiang held power, arrogant as nobles; only toward Yuan did they show respect.

sentences.zh: 原朝會衣青袍，亨笑曰：「行為先生易之。

translations.literal: At court Yuan wore green robes; Heng laughed and said: "I shall have it changed for the gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: At court Yuan wore green robes; Heng laughed and said: "I shall have that changed for you, sir."

sentences.zh: 」原不答。

translations.literal: Yuan did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan did not answer.

sentences.zh: 尋與嶽正列亨、吉祥罪狀，疏留中。

translations.literal: Soon with Yue Zheng he listed the crimes of Heng and Jixiang; the memorial was retained at court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with Yue Zheng, he listed the crimes of Heng and Jixiang; the memorial was retained at court.

sentences.zh: 二人怒，摘敕諭中語，謂閣臣謗訕。

translations.literal: The two men were angry, picked phrases from the imperial patent, and said the cabinet ministers had slandered them.
translations.idiomatic: The two men were angry, picked phrases from the imperial patent, and said the cabinet ministers had slandered them.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，坐便殿，召對，厲聲曰：「正大膽敢爾！

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered, sat in the convenient hall, summoned them to audience, and in a harsh voice said: "Zheng is bold to dare this!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly angered, sat in the convenient hall, summoned them to audience, and in a harsh voice said: "Zheng is bold to dare this!"

sentences.zh: 原素恭謹，阿正何也？

translations.literal: Yuan is always respectful and cautious—why fawn on Zheng?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan is always respectful and cautious—why fawn on Zheng?

sentences.zh: 」正罷去，原得留。

translations.literal: Zheng was dismissed and left; Yuan was kept.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was dismissed and withdrew; Yuan was kept on.

sentences.zh: 李賢既復官入閣柄政，原佐之。

translations.literal: When Li Xian was restored to office and entered the cabinet to direct government, Yuan assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xian was restored to office and entered the cabinet to direct government, Yuan assisted him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，彭時亦入，三人相得甚歡。

translations.literal: Before long Peng Shi also entered; the three men got along very well together.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Peng Shi also entered the cabinet; the three men got along very well together.

sentences.zh: 賢通達，遇事立斷。

translations.literal: Xian was perspicacious and when affairs arose decided at once.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was perspicacious and decided affairs at once when they arose.

sentences.zh: 原濟以持重，庶政稱理。

translations.literal: Yuan assisted with steadiness; general administration was said to be well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan assisted with steadiness; general administration was said to be well ordered.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，進翰林院學士。

translations.literal: That winter he was promoted Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 六年，遭母喪，水漿不入口三日。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he suffered his mother's death and took no water or broth for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he suffered his mother's death and took no water or broth for three days.

sentences.zh: 詔葬畢即起視事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that when burial was complete he immediately return to office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that when burial was complete he immediately return to office.

sentences.zh: 原乞終制。

translations.literal: Yuan begged to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan begged to complete the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: This was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: This was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 乃之景州，啟父兄殯歸葬，舟中寢苫哀毀。

translations.literal: He then went to Jingzhou, opened the coffins of father and brother and returned them for burial; on the boat he slept on the mourning mat in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Jingzhou, opened the coffins of his father and brother and returned them for burial; on the boat he slept on the mourning mat in grief.

sentences.zh: 體素豐，至是羸瘠。

translations.literal: His constitution had always been robust; by now he was emaciated.
translations.idiomatic: His constitution had always been robust; by now he was emaciated.

sentences.zh: 抵家甫襄事而卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: Arriving home he had just finished the funeral rites when he died, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Arriving home he had just finished the funeral rites when he died, aged forty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部左侍郎，謚文懿。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Left Vice Minister of Rites, posthumous name Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted left vice minister of rites, with the posthumous name Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 原內剛外和，與物無競。

translations.literal: Yuan was inwardly firm and outwardly gentle, contending with no one.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was inwardly firm and outwardly gentle, contending with no one.

sentences.zh: 性儉約，身無紈綺。

translations.literal: By nature frugal and abstemious, on his person he had no silk finery.
translations.idiomatic: By nature frugal and abstemious, he wore no silk finery on his person.

sentences.zh: 歸裝惟賜衣數襲，分祿恤宗姻。

translations.literal: His return baggage held only several suits of bestowed garments; he divided his salary to comfort kinsmen by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His return baggage held only several suits of bestowed garments; he divided his salary to support kinsmen by marriage.

sentences.zh: 子常，字秉之。

translations.literal: Zichang, style name Bingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zichang, whose style was Bingzhi.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補國子生，供事翰林，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: By yin privilege made a student of the National University, served the Hanlin, was promoted Secretary of the Secretariat Chancery.
translations.idiomatic: By yin privilege he became a student of the National University, served in the Hanlin, and was promoted secretary of the Secretariat Chancery.

sentences.zh: 疏乞應試，所司執故事不許。

translations.literal: He memorialized begging to sit the examinations; the department held to precedent and would not permit.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking to sit the examinations; the department held to precedent and would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 憲宗特許之，遂舉順天鄉試。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong specially permitted it; he thereupon passed the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong specially permitted it; he thereupon passed the Shuntian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 舍人得赴試自常始。

translations.literal: Secretaries of the Chancery permitted to sit examinations began with Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Secretaries of the Chancery being permitted to sit examinations began with Chang.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部郎中，好學能文，諳掌故。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites; he loved learning and could write, versed in institutional precedents.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites; he loved learning, wrote well, and was versed in institutional precedents.

sentences.zh: 琉球請歲一入貢，回回貢使乞道廣東歸國，皆以非制格之。

translations.literal: Ryukyu requested yearly tribute once; Muslim tribute envoys begged to return home by way of Guangdong—all were rejected as contrary to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Ryukyu requested annual tribute once; Muslim tribute envoys asked to return home by way of Guangdong—all were rejected as contrary to statute.

sentences.zh: 以薦進南京太仆寺少卿。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was advanced to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was advanced to vice director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 故事，太仆馬數，不令他官知。

translations.literal: By precedent the number of horses in the Imperial Stud was not to be known to other officials.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the number of horses in the Imperial Stud was not to be known to other officials.

sentences.zh: 以是文籍磨滅，登耗無稽。

translations.literal: For this reason documents were worn away and registers of gain and loss had no basis.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason documents were worn away and registers of gain and loss had no reliable basis.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「他官不與聞，是也；

translations.literal: Chang said: "That other officials should not hear of it is right;"
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "That other officials should not hear of it is right;"

sentences.zh: 當職者，可貿貿耶？

translations.literal: but for those holding the office, can they be indifferent?
translations.idiomatic: but for those holding the office, can they be indifferent?

sentences.zh: 」議請三年一校勘，著為例。

translations.literal: He proposed triennial collation and established this as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed triennial collation and established this as precedent.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京太常卿，輯《典故因革》若干卷。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he compiled several volumes of Institutional Changes and Reforms.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to minister of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices and compiled several volumes of Institutional Changes and Reforms.

sentences.zh: 正德初，致仕歸。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengde he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengde he retired.

sentences.zh: 嶽正，字季方，漷縣人。

translations.literal: Yue Zheng, style name Jifang, was a man of Huo county.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Zheng, whose style was Jifang, came from Huo county.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年會試第一，賜進士及第，授編修，進左贊善。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he ranked first in the metropolitan examination, was granted jinshi with highest honors, appointed Compiler, promoted Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he ranked first in the metropolitan examination, was granted jinshi with highest honors, appointed compiler, and promoted left assistant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 天順初，改修撰，教小內侍書。

translations.literal: Early in Tianshun he was changed to Reviser and taught the young palace attendants writing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianshun he was transferred to reviser and taught the young palace attendants writing.

sentences.zh: 閣臣徐有貞、李賢下獄，帝既用呂原預政，頃之，薛瑄又致仕，帝謀代者。

translations.literal: Cabinet ministers Xu Youzhen and Li Xian were imprisoned; the Emperor had already used Lu Yuan to share in government; soon Xue Xuan also retired—the Emperor sought a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Cabinet ministers Xu Youzhen and Li Xian were imprisoned; the Emperor had already used Lu Yuan to share in government; soon Xue Xuan also retired, and the Emperor sought a replacement.

sentences.zh: 王翺以正薦，遂召見文華殿。

translations.literal: Wang Ao recommended Zheng; he was thereupon summoned to audience in Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao recommended Zheng; he was thereupon summoned to audience in the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 正長身美須髯，帝遙見，色喜。

translations.literal: Zheng was tall with a fine beard; seen from afar the Emperor's expression brightened.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was tall with a fine beard; seen from afar the Emperor's expression brightened.

sentences.zh: 既登陛，連稱善。

translations.literal: Having mounted the steps he repeatedly said "Excellent."
translations.idiomatic: Having mounted the steps he repeatedly said "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 問年幾何，家安在，何年進士，正具以對。

translations.literal: Asked his age, where his family was, what year he became jinshi—Zheng answered in full.
translations.idiomatic: Asked his age, where his family was, and what year he became jinshi—Zheng answered in full.

sentences.zh: 復大喜曰：「爾年正強仕，吾北人，又吾所取士，今用爾內閣，其盡力輔朕。

translations.literal: Again greatly pleased, he said: "Your years are exactly in full vigor; I am a northerner, and moreover you are one whom I selected as a scholar-official. Now I employ you in the Grand Secretariat—exert all your strength in assisting Me."
translations.idiomatic: He was again greatly pleased and said, "You are in the prime of life; I am a northerner, and you are a man I chose through the examinations. I am putting you in the Grand Secretariat—serve Me with all your strength."

sentences.zh: 」正頓首受命。

translations.literal: " Zheng kowtowed and accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng kowtowed and accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 趨出，石亨、張軏遇之左順門，愕然曰：「何自至此？

translations.literal: Hurrying out, at Zuoshun Gate he met Shi Heng and Zhang Yu, who startled said: "From where did you come here?"
translations.idiomatic: As he hurried out, Shi Heng and Zhang Yu met him at Zuoshun Gate. Startled, they said, "How did you get here?"

sentences.zh: 」比入，帝曰：「朕今日自擇一閣臣。

translations.literal: " When they entered, the Emperor said: "Today I personally chose one Grand Secretary."
translations.idiomatic: " When they entered, the Emperor said, "Today I chose a Grand Secretary myself."

sentences.zh: 」問為誰，帝曰：「嶽正。

translations.literal: " Asked who it was, the Emperor said: "Yue Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: " When asked who, the Emperor said, "Yue Zheng."

sentences.zh: 」兩人陽賀。

translations.literal: " The two men offered false congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: " The two men feigned congratulations.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「但官小耳，當與吏部左侍郎兼學士。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Only his rank is small—he should be given Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel concurrently as Academician."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "His rank is merely low; he should be given the post of left vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel with concurrent appointment as Academician."

sentences.zh: 」兩人曰：「陛下既得人，俟稱職，加秩未晚。

translations.literal: " The two men said: "Your Majesty has already obtained a man; wait until he proves equal to the office—raising his rank will not be late."
translations.idiomatic: " They said, "Your Majesty has found his man; wait until he proves himself in office—it will not be too late to promote him then."

sentences.zh: 」帝默然，遂命以原官入閣。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was silent, and thereupon ordered him to enter the Grand Secretariat at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said nothing and ordered Zheng to join the Grand Secretariat at his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 正素豪邁，負氣敢言。

translations.literal: Zheng by nature was bold and forthright, proud in spirit and daring in speech.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had always been bold and high-spirited, unafraid to speak his mind.

sentences.zh: 及為帝所拔擢，益感激思自效。

translations.literal: When promoted by the Emperor, he was all the more grateful and resolved to repay with loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Emperor raised him up, he grew all the more grateful and eager to prove himself.

sentences.zh: 掌欽天監侍郎湯序者，亨黨也，嘗奏災異，請盡去奸臣。

translations.literal: Tang Xu, who supervised the Directorate of Astronomy as Vice Minister, was of Heng's faction; he once memorialized on calamities and portents, requesting that all treacherous ministers be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xu of the Directorate of Astronomy, a vice minister and member of Heng's faction, once memorialized about omens and disasters, asking that all corrupt ministers be swept away.

sentences.zh: 帝問正，正言：「奸臣無指名。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Zheng; Zheng said: "Treacherous ministers are not named.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Zheng, who replied, "No corrupt ministers are named.

sentences.zh: 即求之，人人自危。

translations.literal: If one seeks them, everyone will feel himself in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Once a hunt begins, every man will fear for himself.

sentences.zh: 且序術淺，何足信也。

translations.literal: Moreover Xu's art is shallow—how could it be worth trusting?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Xu's learning is shallow—hardly something to credit.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 有僧為妖言，錦衣校邏得之，坐以謀反。

translations.literal: A monk spread demonic talk; a Jinyi Guard corporal seized him by pursuit and convicted him of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: A monk was spreading seditious rumors; a corporal of the Embroidered Uniform Guard tracked him down and had him convicted of treason.

sentences.zh: 中官牛玉請官邏者，正言：「事縱得實，不過坐妖言律，邏者給賞而已，不宜與官。

translations.literal: The eunuch Niu Yu requested office for the pursuer; Zheng said: "Even if the matter proved true, the crime would at most fall under the statute on demonic talk—the pursuer should receive a reward only, and ought not be given office."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Niu Yu asked that the pursuer be given an official post; Zheng said, "Even if the charges were true, this would at most be a case under the law against seditious speech—the pursuer should receive a bounty, not an appointment."

sentences.zh: 」僧黨數十人皆得免。

translations.literal: " Several dozen members of the monk's faction all obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: " Dozens of the monk's associates were all spared.

sentences.zh: 或為匿名書列曹吉祥罪狀，吉祥怒，請出榜購之。

translations.literal: Someone wrote an anonymous letter listing Cao Jixiang's crimes; Jixiang grew angry and requested that a public notice be posted offering a reward for the writer's capture.
translations.idiomatic: Someone posted an anonymous letter detailing Cao Jixiang's offenses; enraged, Jixiang asked that a reward notice be posted to hunt the author down.

sentences.zh: 帝使正撰榜格，正與呂原入見曰：「為政有體，盜賊責兵部，奸宄責法司，豈有天子出榜購募者？

translations.literal: The Emperor had Zheng draft the notice format; Zheng and Lu Yuan entered audience and said: "Governance has its proper form—bandits and robbers are the responsibility of the Ministry of War, treacherous wrongdoers of the judicial offices; how could the Son of Heaven ever post a public notice offering a reward?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Zheng draft the reward notice; Zheng and Lu Yuan came before him and said, "Government has its proper channels—bandits belong to the Ministry of War, subversives to the courts. Would a Son of Heaven really post a bounty notice?"

sentences.zh: 且事緩之則自露，急之則愈匿，此人情也。

translations.literal: Moreover if a matter is slackened it will expose itself; if pressed it will be hidden all the more—such is human nature.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, if you leave it alone the truth will come out; press it and men will only hide deeper—that is human nature.

sentences.zh: 」帝是其言，不問。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved his words and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 亨從子彪鎮大同，獻捷，下內閣問狀。

translations.literal: Heng's nephew's son Biao, stationed at Datong, submitted a victory report; it was sent down to the Grand Secretariat to inquire into the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's nephew Biao, commanding at Datong, sent in a victory report, which the Grand Secretariat was asked to verify.

sentences.zh: 使者言捕斬無算，不能悉致，皆梟置林木間。

translations.literal: The emissary said those captured and beheaded were beyond counting and could not all be brought; all were displayed on poles among the trees.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy claimed uncountable kills and beheadings, said they could not all be transported, and that the heads had been impaled among the woods.

sentences.zh: 正按地圖指詰之，曰：「某地至某地，皆沙漠，汝梟置何所？

translations.literal: Zheng consulted the map and pointed while questioning him, saying: "From such-and-such place to such-and-such place—all desert; where did you display them on poles?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng spread out a map and pressed him: "From here to here it is all desert—where did you put those impaled heads?"

sentences.zh: 」其人語塞。

translations.literal: " That man was speechless.
translations.idiomatic: " The man could not answer.

sentences.zh: 時亨、吉祥恣甚，帝頗厭之。

translations.literal: At the time Heng and Jixiang were extremely willful; the Emperor was rather weary of them.
translations.idiomatic: By then Heng and Jixiang had grown insufferably powerful, and the Emperor had begun to tire of them.

sentences.zh: 正從容言：「二人權太重，臣請以計間之。

translations.literal: Zheng calmly said: "Those two men's power is too heavy; your subject requests to estrange them by stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said calmly, "Those two wield too much power; allow me to drive a wedge between them."

sentences.zh: 」帝許焉。

translations.literal: " The Emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 正出見吉祥曰：「忠國公常令杜清來此何為者？

translations.literal: Zheng went out and, meeting Jixiang, said: "The Loyal Duke often sends Du Qing here—what for?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng went out and told Jixiang, "The Loyal Duke keeps sending Du Qing here—what is he after?"

sentences.zh: 」吉祥曰：「辱石公愛，致誠款耳。

translations.literal: " Jixiang said: "It shames me to receive Lord Shi's affection—he merely shows sincere goodwill."
translations.idiomatic: " Jixiang replied, "Lord Shi favors me—that is all; he means it in goodwill."

sentences.zh: 」正曰：「不然，彼使伺公所為耳。

translations.literal: " Zheng said: "Not so—he sends men to watch what you do."
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng said, "Not at all—he is having you watched."

sentences.zh: 」因勸吉祥辭兵柄。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he urged Jixiang to relinquish military power.
translations.idiomatic: " He urged Jixiang to give up his military authority.

sentences.zh: 復詣亨，諭令自戢。

translations.literal: He again went to Heng and instructed him to restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Heng and told him to keep himself in check.

sentences.zh: 亨、吉祥揣知正意，怒。

translations.literal: Heng and Jixiang guessed Zheng's intent and grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and Jixiang saw through Zheng's scheme and flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 吉祥見帝，免冠，泣請死。

translations.literal: Jixiang saw the Emperor, removed his cap, wept, and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang went before the Emperor, removed his cap, wept, and begged to die.

sentences.zh: 帝內愧，慰諭之，召正責漏言。

translations.literal: The Emperor inwardly felt shame, comforted and instructed him, and summoned Zheng to reprove him for leaking speech.
translations.idiomatic: Mortified, the Emperor comforted Jixiang, then summoned Zheng and rebuked him for letting the scheme slip.

sentences.zh: 會承天門災，正極言亨將為不軌，且言：「陳汝言，小人。

translations.literal: It happened that Chengtian Gate burned; Zheng spoke forcefully that Heng was about to act improperly, and further said: "Chen Ruyan is a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengtian Gate caught fire, Zheng insisted that Heng was plotting treason and added, "Chen Ruyan is a small-minded man.

sentences.zh: 今既為尚書，可用盧彬為侍郎。

translations.literal: Now that he is already Minister, Lu Bin may be used as Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He is already minister of a ministry—appoint Lu Bin as vice minister instead.

sentences.zh: 二人者俱譎悍，若同事必相齮龁，乘其隙可並去之。

translations.literal: Both men are crafty and fierce; if they serve together they will surely bite at each other—seizing the opening, both may be removed together.
translations.idiomatic: Both are cunning and fierce; put them together and they will tear at each other—we can use that opening to get rid of both.

sentences.zh: 」徐有貞再下獄，復云：「用有貞則天變可弭。

translations.literal: " Xu Youzhen was again sent down to prison; Zheng again said: "Employ Youzhen and the heaven-sent change may be stilled."
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Youzhen was back in prison; Zheng added, "Restore Xu Youzhen and Heaven's warning may subside."

sentences.zh: 」帝皆不納。

translations.literal: " The Emperor accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor rejected every suggestion.

sentences.zh: 及敕諭廷臣，命正視草。

translations.literal: When an imperial instruction was to admonish the court officials, the Emperor ordered Zheng to inspect the draft.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict was to be issued to the court, the Emperor put Zheng in charge of drafting it.

sentences.zh: 正草敕曰：「乃者承天門災，朕心震驚，罔知所措。

translations.literal: Zheng drafted the edict, saying: "Recently Chengtian Gate suffered disaster; My heart is shaken and alarmed, and I know not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng drafted the edict: "Recently Chengtian Gate was destroyed by fire; I am shaken and do not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 意敬天事神，有未盡歟？

translations.literal: Might revering Heaven and serving the spirits have been incomplete?
translations.idiomatic: Have I failed in reverence toward Heaven and the spirits?

sentences.zh: 祖宗成憲有不遵歟？

translations.literal: Might the established statutes of the ancestors have gone unobserved?
translations.idiomatic: Have I departed from the lasting institutions of my forefathers?

sentences.zh: 善惡不分，用舍乖歟？

translations.literal: Good and evil undistinguished, appointment and dismissal perverse?
translations.idiomatic: Have good and evil been confused, and appointments and dismissals gone wrong?

sentences.zh: 曲直不辨，刑獄冤歟？

translations.literal: Right and wrong unadjudicated, punishments and prisons unjust?
translations.idiomatic: Have right and wrong gone undecided, leaving trials and prisons filled with injustice?

sentences.zh: 征調多方，軍旅勞歟？

translations.literal: Levies and requisitions in many directions, armies and expeditions weary?
translations.idiomatic: Have levies and requisitions been too many, wearing out the armies?

sentences.zh: 賞賚無度，府庫虛歟？

translations.literal: Rewards and grants without measure, treasuries and storehouses empty?
translations.idiomatic: Have rewards been dispensed without limit, draining the treasury?

sentences.zh: 請謁不息，官爵濫歟？

translations.literal: Petition and solicitation unceasing, offices and ranks bestowed recklessly?
translations.idiomatic: Have favor-seeking never ceased, and offices and titles been handed out too freely?

sentences.zh: 賄賂公行，政事廢歟？

translations.literal: Bribes openly practiced, government affairs abandoned?
translations.idiomatic: Has bribery run rampant while affairs of state stagnate?

sentences.zh: 朋奸欺罔，附權勢歟？

translations.literal: Factional villains deceiving and misleading, clinging to power and influence?
translations.idiomatic: Have corrupt factions deceived me, clinging to the powerful?

sentences.zh: 群吏弄法，擅威福歟？

translations.literal: Officials in masses manipulate the law, arrogating intimidation and favor?
translations.idiomatic: Have clerks twisted the law to wield power on their own?

sentences.zh: 征斂徭役太重，而閭閻靡寧歟？

translations.literal: Taxation and corvée too heavy, while lanes and hamlets know no peace?
translations.idiomatic: Have taxes and corvée labor been too burdensome, leaving neighborhoods without rest?

sentences.zh: 讒諂奔競之徒幸進，而忠言正士不用歟？

translations.literal: Slanderers, flatterers, and scheming strivers gain favor and advancement, while loyal words and upright gentlemen go unused?
translations.idiomatic: Have sycophants and office-seekers risen while loyal and upright men have been ignored?

sentences.zh: 抑有司阘茸酷暴，貪冒無厭，而致軍民不得其所歟？

translations.literal: Or is it that officials are incompetent, cruel, and violent, greedy and insatiable, causing soldiers and people not to obtain their proper place?
translations.idiomatic: Or have local officials been corrupt, cruel, and insatiable, so that soldiers and civilians have nowhere to turn?

sentences.zh: 此皆傷和致災之由，而朕有所未明也。

translations.literal: These are all causes that wound harmony and bring disaster, whereas I have points I do not yet understand.
translations.idiomatic: All these disrupt harmony and bring calamity—yet I cannot see clearly where the fault lies.

sentences.zh: 今朕省愆思咎，怵惕是存。

translations.literal: Now I examine faults and contemplate blame; fear and caution are what I keep.
translations.idiomatic: Now I examine my errors and search my conscience, living in watchful dread.

sentences.zh: 爾群臣休戚惟均，其洗心改過，無蹈前非，當行者直言無隱。

translations.literal: You officials share joy and sorrow alike; wash your hearts and reform faults, do not tread former wrongs—those who ought to speak, speak straightforwardly without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: You ministers share my fate; cleanse your hearts, mend your ways, and do not repeat past errors—where speech is owed, speak plainly and hold nothing back.

sentences.zh: 」敕下，舉朝傳誦。

translations.literal: " When the edict was issued, the whole court passed it around reciting it.
translations.idiomatic: " When the edict went out, the entire court read and recited it.

sentences.zh: 而亨、吉祥構蜚語，謂正賣直謗訕。

translations.literal: But Heng and Jixiang fabricated slanderous talk, saying Zheng was selling integrity and reviling with insult.
translations.idiomatic: But Heng and Jixiang spread rumors that Zheng was grandstanding and slandering the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命仍授內侍書。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew angry and ordered that he again be assigned to teach the young eunuchs' writing.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage and ordered Zheng back to teaching the young eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 明日，謫欽州同知。

translations.literal: The next day he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was demoted to vice prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 道漷，以母老留旬日。

translations.literal: Passing through Huo, because his mother was old he remained ten days.
translations.idiomatic: On his way he passed through Huo and stayed ten days to see his aging mother.

sentences.zh: 陳汝言令巡校言狀，且言正嘗奪公主田。

translations.literal: Chen Ruyan had patrol guards report his conduct, and further said Zheng had once seized the princess's fields.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ruyan had patrol guards inform on him and added that Zheng had once seized land belonging to a princess.

sentences.zh: 遂逮系詔獄，杖百，戍肅州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was arrested and held in the Imperial Prison, beaten a hundred strokes, and sent to garrison at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was thrown into the imperial prison, beaten a hundred times, and banished to garrison duty at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 行至涿，夜宿傳舍。

translations.literal: Having traveled as far as Zhuo, by night he lodged at a relay station.
translations.idiomatic: On the road at Zhuo he spent the night at a courier station.

sentences.zh: 手拲急，氣奔且死。

translations.literal: The hand shackles were tight; his breath rushed and he was near death.
translations.idiomatic: His shackles were tight; gasping for breath, he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 涿人楊四醉卒酒，脫正拲，刳其中，且厚賂卒，乃得至戍所。

translations.literal: Yang Si of Zhuo, drunk, got the guards drunk on wine, removed Zheng's shackles, scooped out their interior, and moreover heavily bribed the guards—only then could he reach the garrison post.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhuo townsman named Yang Si got the escorts drunk, removed Zheng's shackles, hollowed them out so they would not bind so cruelly, and bribed the guards heavily before Zheng could reach his post.

sentences.zh: 亨、吉祥既誅，帝謂李賢曰：「嶽正固嘗言之。

translations.literal: After Heng and Jixiang were executed, the Emperor said to Li Xian: "Yue Zheng indeed once spoke of this."
translations.idiomatic: After Heng and Jixiang were put to death, the Emperor told Li Xian, "Yue Zheng had tried to warn me."

sentences.zh: 」賢曰：「正有老母，得放歸田裏，幸甚。

translations.literal: " Xian said: "Zheng has an aged mother; if he could be released to return to the fields, it would be a great fortune."
translations.idiomatic: " Xian said, "Zheng still has an old mother at home; it would be a great mercy to let him go home to his fields."

sentences.zh: 」乃釋為民。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was released as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng was released to live as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，御史呂洪等請復正與楊瑄官，詔正以原官直經筵，纂修《英宗實錄》。

translations.literal: When Xianzong ascended, Censor Lu Hong and others requested restoration of office for Zheng and Yang Xuan; an edict ordered Zheng at his original office to attend the Classics Lectern and compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chenghua Emperor came to the throne, Censor Lu Hong and others asked that Zheng and Yang Xuan be restored to office; an edict recalled Zheng to his former rank to serve at the imperial lectures and help compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Ying.

sentences.zh: 初，正得罪，都督僉事季鐸乞得其宅，至是敕還正。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zheng fell from grace, Regional Commander Vice Commissioner Ji Duo requested to obtain his residence; at this time an edict returned it to Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng first fell, Vice Commissioner Ji Duo of the regional command had asked for his house; now an edict ordered it returned.

sentences.zh: 正還朝，自謂當大用，而賢欲用為南京祭酒，正不悅。

translations.literal: Zheng returned to court, considering himself due for great employment, but Xian wished to appoint him Chancellor of the Nanjing Directorate of Education—Zheng was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng returned expecting a major appointment, but Xian wanted to make him chancellor of the Nanjing Directorate of Education; Zheng was unhappy.

sentences.zh: 忌者偽為正劾賢疏草，賢嗛之。

translations.literal: Envious men forged a draft memorial by Zheng impeaching Xian; Xian harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: His enemies forged a draft memorial in Zheng's name attacking Xian, and Xian took offense.

sentences.zh: 成化元年四月，廷推兵部侍郎清理貼黃，以正與給事中張寧名並上。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Chenghua, the court recommended candidates to examine memorial endorsements as Vice Minister of War; Zheng's name and that of Supervising Secretary Zhang Ning were submitted together.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Chenghua 1, when the court nominated candidates to review memorial endorsements for vice minister of war, Zheng's name and that of Supervising Secretary Zhang Ning were both submitted.

sentences.zh: 詔以為私，出正為興化知府，而寧亦補外。

translations.literal: An edict deemed it factional favoritism; Zheng was sent out as Prefect of Xinghua, and Ning also was assigned outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The throne called it favoritism and sent Zheng out as prefect of Xinghua; Ning was posted outside the capital as well.

sentences.zh: 正至官，築堤溉田數千頃，節縮浮費，經理預備倉，欲有所興革。

translations.literal: When Zheng reached his post, he built dikes and irrigated several thousand qing of fields, cut wasteful expenses, managed the reserve granaries, and wished to undertake reforms.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, Zheng built dikes to irrigate thousands of acres, pared unnecessary spending, reorganized the reserve granaries, and set out to reform local practice.

sentences.zh: 鄉士大夫不利其所為，騰謗言。

translations.literal: Local gentry and officials found his conduct injurious to their interests and raised slanderous talk.
translations.idiomatic: Local gentry who resented his reforms spread malicious rumors.

sentences.zh: 正亦厭吏職，五年入覲，遂致仕。

translations.literal: Zheng also grew weary of official duty; in the fifth year he entered court audience and thereupon retired.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had wearied of office himself; on his fifth-year audience visit he retired.

sentences.zh: 又五年卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: Five years later he died, aged fifty-five.
