translations.idiomatic: Five years after that he died, at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 無子，大學士李東陽、御史李經，其婿也。

translations.literal: He had no son; Grand Secretary Li Dongyang and Censor Li Jing were his sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; his sons-in-law were Grand Secretary Li Dongyang and Censor Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 正博學能文章，高自期許，氣屹屹不能下人。

translations.literal: Zheng was broadly learned and able in literary composition, setting high expectations for himself; his spirit stood towering and could not defer to others.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was learned and a strong writer, ambitious and proud, with a bearing that bowed to no one.

sentences.zh: 在內閣才二十八日，勇事敢言，便殿論奏，至唾濺帝衣。

translations.literal: In the Grand Secretariat only twenty-eight days, he courageously served and dared speak; in the informal hall he debated and memorialized, until spittle splashed the Emperor's robe.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Grand Secretariat only twenty-eight days, yet spoke boldly even in the privy council—once so vehemently that spittle flecked the Emperor's robe.

sentences.zh: 有規以信而後諫者，慨然曰：「上顧我厚，懼無以報稱，子乃以諫官處我耶？

translations.literal: Someone who admonished him to trust first and then remonstrate sighed and said: "The Emperor treats me generously; I fear I have no way to repay—you treat me as a remonstrating official?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged him to wait until he had the Emperor's trust before pushing so hard, he replied indignantly, "The Emperor has shown me such favor that I fear I can never repay it—and you would have me behave like a hired remonstrator?"

sentences.zh: 」英宗亦悉其忠，其在戍所，嘗念之曰：「嶽正倒好，只是大膽。

translations.literal: " Emperor Ying also fully knew his loyalty; while he was at the garrison post, he once recalled him saying: "Yue Zheng is really quite good—only too bold."
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Ying knew his loyalty well; while Zheng was in exile he once mused, "Yue Zheng is a good man—just far too bold."

sentences.zh: 」正聞自為像贊，述帝前語，末言：「臣嘗聞古人之言，蓋將之死而靡憾也。

translations.literal: Zheng heard of this and composed his own portrait eulogy, reciting the Emperor's earlier words; at the end he wrote: "Your subject has heard the words of the ancients—that one who is about to die has no regrets."
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng heard of this he wrote an inscription for his own portrait quoting the Emperor and closing with, "I have heard the ancients say that a man facing death should have no regrets."

sentences.zh: 」其自信不回如此。

translations.literal: " Such was his steadfast self-confidence.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was his unshakable self-conviction.

sentences.zh: 然意廣才疏，欲以縱橫之術離散權黨，反為所噬，人皆迂而惜之。

translations.literal: Yet his aims were broad and his talent narrow; wishing to use divisive stratagems to scatter the power faction, he was instead devoured by them—men all considered him impractical yet pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his vision outran his skill: he tried to break up the power blocs with divide-and-rule tactics and was destroyed instead; most saw him as quixotic and regretted his fate.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，追贈太常寺卿，謚文肅。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing reign he was posthumously made minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 彭時，字純道，安福人。

translations.literal: Peng Shi, style name Chundao, was a man of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shi, whose style was Chundao, came from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進士第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he ranked first among jinshi and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 13 he topped the jinshi examination and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 明年，郕王監國，令同商輅入閣預機務。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Prince of Cheng acted as regent, he was ordered together with Shang Lu to enter the Grand Secretariat and participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the Prince of Cheng became regent, he and Shang Lu were brought into the Grand Secretariat to share in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 聞繼母憂，力辭，不允，乃拜命。

translations.literal: On hearing of his stepmother's mourning he forcefully declined; it was not permitted, and only then did he accept the command.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned his stepmother had died, he tried hard to decline; refused, he finally accepted.

sentences.zh: 釋褐逾年參大政，前此未有也。

translations.literal: Shedding plain cloth and within a year participating in great governance—before this there had never been such a case.
translations.idiomatic: To enter high office within a year of leaving student robes was without precedent.

sentences.zh: 尋進侍讀。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，以兵事稍息，得請終制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, because military affairs had slightly subsided, he obtained permission to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1, with the fighting dying down, he was allowed to finish his mourning period.

sentences.zh: 然由此忤旨。

translations.literal: Yet because of this he went against the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: By this he fell out of the Emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 服除，命供事翰林院，不復與閣事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was ordered to serve at the Hanlin Academy and no longer participate in Grand Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period he was assigned to the Hanlin Academy and barred from Grand Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 易儲，遷左春坊大學士。

translations.literal: When the heir was changed, he was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Left Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the change of crown prince he was moved to grand tutor of the Left Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 《寰宇通志》成，遷太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: When the 《Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm》 was completed, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On completion of the 《Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm》, he became vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 俱兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Both offices were held concurrently with Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He held both posts while also serving as reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 天順元年，徐有貞既得罪，嶽正、許彬相繼罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun, after Xu Youzhen had fallen into disgrace, Yue Zheng and Xu Bin were dismissed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 1, Xu Youzhen was already ruined; Yue Zheng and Xu Bin were dismissed one after another.

sentences.zh: 帝坐文華殿召見時，曰：「汝非朕所擢狀元乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor, seated in the Wenhua Hall, summoned Shi for audience and said: "Are you not the top jinshi whom I myself elevated?"
translations.idiomatic: Seated in Wenhua Hall, the Emperor summoned Shi and asked, "Aren't you the jinshi champion I personally promoted?"

sentences.zh: 」時頓首。

translations.literal: " Shi kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi prostrated himself.

sentences.zh: 明日仍命入閣，兼翰林院學士。

translations.literal: The next day he was again ordered to enter the Grand Secretariat, concurrently as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was restored to the Grand Secretariat as Hanlin academician as well.

sentences.zh: 閣臣自三楊後，進退禮甚輕。

translations.literal: Since the Three Yang, grand secretaries' rites of appointment and dismissal had been very slight.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Yang, elevation to and removal from the Grand Secretariat had counted for little.

sentences.zh: 為帝所親擢者，唯時與正二人。

translations.literal: Those personally elevated by the Emperor were only Shi and Zheng, two men.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shi and Zheng had been personally chosen by the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 而帝方向用李賢，數召賢獨對。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor was then inclined to employ Li Xian, summoning Xian alone for private consultation many times.
translations.idiomatic: But the Emperor now favored Li Xian and often summoned him for private counsel.

sentences.zh: 賢雅重時，退必咨之。

translations.literal: Xian greatly respected Shi by nature; on retiring he always consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian held Shi in high esteem and always sought his advice after audience.

sentences.zh: 時引義爭可否，或至失色。

translations.literal: Shi, citing principle, disputed what should or should not be done, sometimes even to the point of changing color.
translations.idiomatic: Shi would cite principle to argue yes or no, sometimes until faces flushed with anger.

sentences.zh: 賢初小忤，久亦服其諒直，曰：「彭公，真君子也。

translations.literal: Xian at first took slight offense; over time he also came to admire his candor and forthrightness, saying: "Lord Peng is a true gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian was briefly annoyed, but in time came to respect his frankness: "Lord Peng is the real article."

sentences.zh: 」慈壽皇太后上尊號，詔告天下。

translations.literal: " When the Empress Dowager Cishou received an honorific title, an edict was proclaimed to all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " When Empress Dowager Cishou was granted an honorific title, an edict announced it to the realm.

sentences.zh: 時欲推恩，賢謂一年不宜再赦。

translations.literal: Shi wished to extend grace; Xian said that within one year it was not appropriate to grant amnesty again.
translations.idiomatic: Shi proposed a broader act of grace; Li Xian argued that two amnesties in one year would be unwise.

sentences.zh: 時曰：「非赦也，宜行優老典。

translations.literal: Shi said: "It is not amnesty; the proper thing is to carry out the rites honoring the aged."
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, "This isn't an amnesty—we should observe the rites for honoring the elderly."

sentences.zh: 朝臣父母七十與誥敕，百姓八十給冠帶，是『老吾老以及人之老』也。

translations.literal: If a court official's parents reach seventy, grant them patent letters; if common people reach eighty, grant them caps and sashes—this is "honoring my own aged and extending that honor to the aged of others."
translations.idiomatic: Patent letters for officials whose parents reach seventy, caps and sashes for commoners at eighty—that is what it means to "honor one's own elders and extend that honor to others' elders."

sentences.zh: 」賢稱善，即奏行之。

translations.literal: " Xian praised it as good and immediately memorialized to put it into practice.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xian approved and had the policy memorialized and enacted.

sentences.zh: 帝愛時風度，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: The Emperor loved Shi's bearing and deportment, and selected junior Hanlin scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admired Shi's bearing and was selecting new Hanlin fellows.

sentences.zh: 命賢盡用北人，南人必若時者方可。

translations.literal: He ordered Xian to employ northerners entirely; southerners could be used only if they were men like Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He told Li Xian to take only northerners; southerners were acceptable only if they were Shi's equal.

sentences.zh: 賢以語時。

translations.literal: Xian told this to Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian relayed this to Shi.

sentences.zh: 俄中官牛玉宣旨，時謂玉曰：「南士出時上者不少，何可抑之？

translations.literal: Soon the eunuch Niu Yu proclaimed the imperial will; Shi said to Yu: "Not a few southern scholars have ranked above Shi—how can they be suppressed?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon the eunuch Niu Yu delivered the edict; Shi told him, "Many southern scholars have outranked me—how can we hold them back?"

sentences.zh: 」已，選十五人，南六人與焉。

translations.literal: " Soon after, fifteen were selected, with six southerners among them.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end fifteen were chosen, six of them southerners.

sentences.zh: 門達構賢，帝惑之，曰：「去賢，行專用時矣。

translations.literal: Men Da framed Xian; the Emperor was misled and said: "Remove Xian, and then I can rely exclusively on Shi."
translations.idiomatic: Men Da slandered Li Xian; the Emperor was taken in and said, "Dismiss Xian, and I'll rely on Shi alone."

sentences.zh: 」或傳其語，時矍然曰：「李公有經濟才，何可去？

translations.literal: " When someone passed on these words, Shi started in alarm and said: "Lord Li has talent for governing—how can he be removed?"
translations.idiomatic: " When word reached him, Shi exclaimed, "Lord Li has real administrative talent—he mustn't go!"

sentences.zh: 」因力直之。

translations.literal: " He therefore forcefully spoke in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore argued strenuously on Li Xian's behalf.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「賢去，時不得獨留。

translations.literal: He also said: "If Xian goes, Shi cannot remain alone."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "If Li Xian goes, I cannot stay on alone."

sentences.zh: 」語聞，帝意乃解。

translations.literal: " When these words were heard, the Emperor's mind was then cleared.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor heard this and changed his mind.

sentences.zh: 帝大漸，口占遺命，定後妃名分，勿以嬪禦殉葬，凡四事，付閣臣潤色。

translations.literal: The Emperor's illness worsened sharply; he orally dictated his final commands, settling the ranks of consorts, forbidding concubines and palace women from being buried alive with him—in all four matters, entrusted to grand secretaries to polish the wording.
translations.idiomatic: As the Emperor lay near death, he dictated his final wishes: fixing the status of the consorts and forbidding palace women from being buried with him—four points in all, left to the grand secretaries to draft properly.

sentences.zh: 時讀竟，涕下，悲愴不自勝。

translations.literal: Shi finished reading and tears fell; grief and distress overwhelmed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi finished reading he wept uncontrollably, overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 中官復命，帝亦為隕涕。

translations.literal: The eunuch reported back; the Emperor also shed tears at it.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch reported back, and the Emperor wept as well.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，議上兩宮尊號。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, they deliberated on bestowing honorific titles on the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong succeeded, the court debated honorific titles for the two empress dowagers.

sentences.zh: 中官夏時希周貴妃旨，言錢後久病，不當稱太后。

translations.literal: The eunuch Xia Shi, seeking to please Noble Consort Zhou, said that Empress Qian had long been ill and ought not be styled Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Xia Shi, currying favor with Noble Consort Zhou, argued that Empress Qian's long illness disqualified her from the title Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 而貴妃，帝所生母，宜獨上尊號。

translations.literal: The noble consort, however, was the Emperor's birth mother and should alone receive an honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: The noble consort, the Emperor's biological mother, alone deserved the honorific title.

sentences.zh: 賢曰：「遺詔已定，何事多言。

translations.literal: Xian said: "The final edict is already fixed—what need for further talk?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian said, "The dying edict has settled this—why reopen it?"

sentences.zh: 」時曰：「李公言是也。

translations.literal: " Shi said: "Lord Li's words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: " Shi agreed: "Lord Li is right."

sentences.zh: 朝廷所以服天下，在正綱常。

translations.literal: The reason the court commands the submission of all under heaven lies in upholding correct ritual norms.
translations.idiomatic: The throne wins obedience by upholding proper ritual and moral order.

sentences.zh: 若不爾，損聖德非小。

translations.literal: If it is not so, harm to sagely virtue will not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the damage to the Emperor's moral standing would be grave.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，中官復傳貴妃旨：「子為皇帝，母當為太后，豈有無子而稱太后者？

translations.literal: " Shortly after, the eunuch again conveyed the noble consort's will: "When the son is emperor, the mother should be empress dowager—how can one without a son be styled empress dowager?"
translations.idiomatic: " Soon the eunuch returned with the consort's message: "An emperor's mother is empress dowager—how can a woman with no son claim that title?"

sentences.zh: 宣德間有故事。

translations.literal: In the Xuande era there was a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Xuande precedent for this.

sentences.zh: 」賢色變，目時。

translations.literal: " Xian changed color and looked at Shi.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xian went pale and looked to Shi.

sentences.zh: 時曰：「今日事與宣德間不同。

translations.literal: Shi said: "Today's affair is not the same as that of the Xuande period."
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, "Today's case isn't the Xuande one."

sentences.zh: 胡後表讓位，退居別宮，故在正統初不加尊。

translations.literal: Empress Hu submitted a memorial ceding her position and withdrew to a separate palace; therefore at the beginning of Zhengtong she was not given an honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Hu had formally abdicated and retired to a separate residence, so she received no honorific at the start of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 今名分固在，安得為比？

translations.literal: Now her title and status are still in place—how can the cases be equated?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qian's status stands firm—there is no comparison.

sentences.zh: 」中官曰：「如是何不草讓表？

translations.literal: " The eunuch said: "If so, why not draft an abdication memorial?"
translations.idiomatic: " The eunuch asked, "Then why not draft an abdication memorial for her?"

sentences.zh: 」時曰：「先帝存日未嘗行，今誰敢草？

translations.literal: " Shi said: "While the late Emperor lived it was never done—who now would dare draft one?"
translations.idiomatic: " Shi answered, "The late Emperor never permitted this in his lifetime—who would dare draft one now?"

sentences.zh: 若人臣阿意順從，是萬世罪人也。

translations.literal: If ministers fawn and comply, they are sinners for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Any minister who toadying complied would be condemned for all time.

sentences.zh: 」中官厲聲怵以危語。

translations.literal: " The eunuch in a harsh voice intimidated with threatening words.
translations.idiomatic: " The eunuch raised his voice and tried to frighten them with threats.

sentences.zh: 時拱手向天曰：「太祖、太宗神靈在上，孰敢有二心！

translations.literal: Shi clasped his hands and, facing heaven, said: "The spirits of Taizu and Taizong are above—who would dare have a second heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi bowed toward heaven and declared, "With the spirits of Taizu and Taizong watching, who would dare dissemble!"

sentences.zh: 錢皇后無子，何所規利而為之爭？

translations.literal: Empress Qian has no son—what profit does she seek that she would struggle for this?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qian had no son—what could she possibly gain by fighting this?

sentences.zh: 臣義不忍默者，欲全主上聖德耳。

translations.literal: The reason your subject by duty cannot bear to keep silent is merely to preserve the sagely virtue of Our Lord above.
translations.idiomatic: I speak because I cannot stay silent if I mean to preserve the Emperor's moral standing.

sentences.zh: 若推大孝之心，則兩宮並尊為宜。

translations.literal: If one extends the heart of great filial piety, then honoring both palaces equally is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: In the spirit of true filial piety, both mothers should receive equal honor.

sentences.zh: 」賢亦極言之，議遂定。

translations.literal: " Xian also spoke to the utmost; the deliberation was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Xian argued just as hard, and the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 及將上寶冊，時曰：「兩宮同稱則無別，錢太后宜加兩字，以便稱謂。

translations.literal: When the imperial patent was about to be presented, Shi said: "If both palaces share the same style there will be no distinction—Empress Dowager Qian should have two additional characters added to facilitate address."
translations.idiomatic: Before the patent was presented, Shi said, "If both bear the same title there'll be no distinction—give Empress Dowager Qian two extra characters for clarity."

sentences.zh: 」乃尊為慈懿皇太后，貴妃為皇太后。

translations.literal: " She was then honored as Empress Dowager Ciyi; the noble consort became Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Qian was styled Empress Dowager Ciyi; the noble consort became Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 越數日，中官覃包至內閣曰：「上意固如是。

translations.literal: Several days later the eunuch Tan Bao came to the Grand Secretariat and said: "His Majesty's mind was indeed thus."
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the eunuch Tan Bao told the Grand Secretariat, "The Emperor had always meant it this way."

sentences.zh: 但迫於太后，不敢自主，非二公力急，幾誤大事。

translations.literal: But pressed by the Empress Dowager, he did not dare decide for himself; had not the two lords pressed urgently, he would nearly have erred greatly in a major affair.
translations.idiomatic: But he bowed to pressure from the empress dowager and didn't dare decide alone—without your forceful stand, a grave mistake would nearly have been made.

sentences.zh: 」時閣臣陳文默無語，聞包言，甚愧。

translations.literal: " At the time Grand Secretary Chen Wen was silent without a word; on hearing Bao's words, he was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Secretary Chen Wen had said nothing throughout; hearing this, he was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 禮成，進吏部右侍郎，兼學士，同知經筵。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently Academician, and shared direction of the Classics Lectern.
translations.idiomatic: After the ceremony he was promoted to right vice minister of personnel, continuing as academician and sharing direction of the imperial lectures.

sentences.zh: 成化改元，進兵部尚書，兼官如故。

translations.literal: When the reign title changed to Chenghua, he was promoted to Minister of War, his concurrent posts remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: With the Chenghua reign he became minister of war, keeping his other posts.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，乞歸省。

translations.literal: The next autumn he requested leave to return home for a family visit.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he asked to visit his family.

sentences.zh: 三年二月詔趣還朝，《英宗實錄》成，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year an edict urgently summoned him back to court; when the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong》 was completed, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Chenghua 3 he was recalled; when the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong》 was finished, he was made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 兼文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: Concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He also became grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 四年，慈懿太后崩，詔議山陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Empress Dowager Ciyi died; an edict ordered deliberation on her mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 4 Empress Dowager Ciyi died, and the court was ordered to plan her burial.

sentences.zh: 時及商輅、劉定之言：「太后作配先帝，正位中宮，陛下尊為太后，詔示天下。

translations.literal: Shi together with Shang Lu and Liu Dingzhi said: "The Empress Dowager was the match of the late Emperor, holding the central position in the Inner Palace; Your Majesty honored her as empress dowager and proclaimed it to all under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Shi, Shang Lu, and Liu Dingzhi argued, "The empress dowager was the late Emperor's lawful consort and rightful empress; you honored her before all the realm."

sentences.zh: 先帝全夫婦之倫，陛下盡母子之愛，於義俱得。

translations.literal: The late Emperor fulfilled the ethics of husband and wife; Your Majesty fulfilled the love between mother and son—in ritual meaning both were satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor kept marital propriety; you have shown filial love—both obligations are met.

sentences.zh: 今梓宮當合葬裕陵，主當祔廟，此不易之禮。

translations.literal: Now her coffin should be jointly buried at Yuling, and her spirit tablet should be enshrined in the ancestral temple—this is the unchanging rite.
translations.idiomatic: Her coffin should be buried with the late Emperor at Yuling and her tablet placed in the ancestral temple—that is immovable custom.

sentences.zh: 比聞欲別卜葬地，臣等實懷疑懼。

translations.literal: Recently we heard that a separate burial site is to be chosen; your ministers truly harbor doubt and fear.
translations.idiomatic: We hear you may choose a separate burial site—that fills us with alarm.

sentences.zh: 竊謂皇上所以遲疑者，必以今皇太后萬壽後，當與先帝同尊，自嫌二後並配，非祖宗制。

translations.literal: We venture to think that the reason Your Majesty hesitates must be that after the present Empress Dowager's long life ends, she will share equal honor with the late Emperor, and you yourself worry that two empresses sharing one match is not the ancestral institution.
translations.idiomatic: We suspect your hesitation stems from concern that when the present empress dowager dies, two empresses would share the late Emperor's tomb—contrary to ancestral custom.

sentences.zh: 考之於古，漢文帝尊所生母薄太后，而呂後仍祔長陵。

translations.literal: Examining antiquity: Emperor Wen of Han honored his birth mother Empress Dowager Bo, yet Empress Lü was still enshrined at Changling.
translations.idiomatic: History shows that Emperor Wen honored his birth mother Empress Dowager Bo, yet Empress Lü remained enshrined at Changling.

sentences.zh: 宋仁宗追尊生母李宸妃，而劉後仍祔太廟。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong of Song posthumously honored his birth mother Consort Li Chenfei, yet Empress Liu was still enshrined in the Great Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Song Renzong elevated his birth mother Consort Li, yet Empress Liu kept her place in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 今若陵廟之制稍有未合，則有乖前美，貽譏來葉。

translations.literal: If now the regulations for tomb and temple are even slightly improper, then former excellence is violated and mockery is bequeathed to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Any deviation from proper tomb and temple rites would betray past precedent and invite posterity's scorn.

sentences.zh: 」於是諸大臣相繼言之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the various great ministers spoke in succession.
translations.idiomatic: " Other senior ministers spoke in turn.

sentences.zh: 帝猶重違太后意，時偕朝臣伏文華門泣請。

translations.literal: The Emperor still heavily feared violating the Empress Dowager's will; Shi together with court officials prostrated themselves at the Wenhua Gate weeping in entreaty.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor still shrank from defying the empress dowager; Shi and other officials knelt weeping at Wenhua Gate to plead.

sentences.zh: 帝與太后皆感動，始從時議。

translations.literal: The Emperor and the Empress Dowager were both moved; he then followed Shi's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor and empress dowager were both moved, and he accepted Shi's counsel.

sentences.zh: 彗見三臺，時等言：「外廷大政固所當先，宮中根本尤為至急。

translations.literal: A comet appeared at Santai; Shi and others said: "Great affairs of the outer court are certainly what should come first, yet the root of the inner palace is especially the most urgent."
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared at Santai, Shi and others warned, "Outer-court governance matters, but the imperial succession is even more urgent."

sentences.zh: 諺雲『子出多母』。

translations.literal: A proverb says, "Many mothers produce many sons."
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, "Many mothers produce many sons."

sentences.zh: 今嬪嬙眾多，維熊無兆。

translations.literal: Now palace women and concubines are numerous, yet no sign of a bear appears.
translations.idiomatic: The harem is crowded, yet no pregnancy has been announced.

sentences.zh: 必陛下愛有所專，而專寵者已過生育之期故也。

translations.literal: It must be that Your Majesty's love is concentrated on one alone, and the one specially favored has already passed the age of childbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Surely Your Majesty favors one woman exclusively—and she is past childbearing age.

sentences.zh: 望均恩愛，為宗社大計。

translations.literal: We hope for equal affection, for the great plan of altars and ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: We urge you to spread your favor equally, for the sake of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 」時帝專寵萬貴妃，妃年已近四十，時故云然。

translations.literal: " At the time the Emperor doted exclusively on Consort Wan; the consort's age was already nearly forty—therefore Shi spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then doted on Consort Wan, who was nearly forty—hence Shi's remark.

sentences.zh: 又言：「大臣黜陟，宜斷自宸衷，或集群臣僉議。

translations.literal: He also said: "The dismissal and promotion of great ministers should be decided from the imperial heart alone, or by assembling the ministers for joint deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged, "Ministerial appointments should be decided by Your Majesty alone—or by full deliberation with the court."

sentences.zh: 不可悉委臣下，使大權旁落。

translations.literal: They cannot all be entrusted to ministers below, causing great power to fall to the side.
translations.idiomatic: Don't delegate everything to subordinates and let power slip away.

sentences.zh: 」帝雖不能從，而心嘉其忠。

translations.literal: " Though the Emperor could not follow this, in his heart he praised his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor couldn't act on it, but admired his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 都御史項忠討滿四不利。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xiang Zhong's campaign against Man Si went badly.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Xiang Zhong's campaign against Man Si was faring poorly.

sentences.zh: 朝議命撫寧侯朱永將京軍往赴。

translations.literal: At court they deliberated ordering the Marquis of Funing Zhu Yong to lead capital troops to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided to send Marquis of Funing Zhu Yong with capital troops to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 永故難其行，多所邀請。

translations.literal: Yong deliberately made difficulty of the expedition, requesting many things.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yong deliberately dragged his feet and made numerous demands.

sentences.zh: 時惡其張大，且度軍可無行，第令整裝待。

translations.literal: Shi despised his grandiosity and also estimated the army need not march; he merely ordered preparations and waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Shi resented his arrogance and judged the army wouldn't need to march—he ordered them merely to stand ready.

sentences.zh: 會忠馳奏，已圍賊石城。

translations.literal: Just then Zhong sent an urgent memorial that he had already besieged the bandits at Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Zhong then reported by express dispatch that he had already besieged the rebels at Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中官懷恩、黃賜偕兵部尚書白圭、程信等至閣議。

translations.literal: The Emperor dispatched the eunuchs Huai'en and Huang Ci together with Minister of War Bai Gui, Cheng Xin, and others to the Grand Secretariat for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent eunuchs Huai'en and Huang Ci with Minister of War Bai Gui and Cheng Xin to the Grand Secretariat to decide.

sentences.zh: 時曰：「賊四出攻剽，鋒誠不可當。

translations.literal: Shi said: "The bandits raid in all directions; their edge truly cannot be withstood."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "The rebels have been raiding everywhere—their momentum was truly hard to stop."

sentences.zh: 今入石城自保，我軍圍甚固，此困獸易擒耳。

translations.literal: Now they have entered Shicheng to protect themselves; our army's siege is very tight—this is a cornered beast, easy to capture.
translations.idiomatic: Now they've holed up in Shicheng under a tight siege—a trapped beast, easily taken.

sentences.zh: 」信曰：「安知忠不退師？

translations.literal: " Xin said: "How do we know Zhong will not withdraw his army?"
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng Xin asked, "How do we know Xiang Zhong won't pull back?"

sentences.zh: 」時曰：「彼部分已定，何故自退？

translations.literal: " Shi said: "Their dispositions are already set—why would they withdraw on their own?"
translations.idiomatic: " Shi replied, "His positions are set—why would he withdraw on his own?"

sentences.zh: 且今出師，度何時到？

translations.literal: Moreover, if troops march out now, estimate when they would arrive?
translations.idiomatic: And if we deploy now, when would reinforcements even arrive?

sentences.zh: 」信曰：「來春。

translations.literal: " Xin said: "Next spring."
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng Xin said, "Not until next spring."

sentences.zh: 」時曰：「如此，益緩不及事。

translations.literal: " Shi said: "If so, that delay would all the more fail to meet the need of the affair."
translations.idiomatic: " Shi said, "By then it would be far too late to matter."

sentences.zh: 事成敗，冬月決矣。

translations.literal: Success or failure in the affair will be decided in the winter months.
translations.idiomatic: Victory or defeat would be settled by winter.

sentences.zh: 」信忿，出危言曰：「忠若敗，必斬一二人，然後出師。

translations.literal: " Xin, angry, spoke alarming words: "If Zhong fails, one or two people must be executed—only then can the army march out."
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng Xin, furious, threw out a grim prediction: "If Xiang Zhong fails, someone's head will roll before any relief force is sent."

sentences.zh: 」眾危之，問時何見。

translations.literal: " All regarded this as alarming and asked Shi what insight he had.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone took this as an omen and asked Shi how he read the situation.

sentences.zh: 曰：「觀忠疏曲折，知其能。

translations.literal: He said: "Examining Zhong's memorial in its detailed turns, I know his competence.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Reading Xiang Zhong's detailed reports, I know he's capable.

sentences.zh: 若聞別遣禁軍，將退避不敢任，賊不可知矣。

translations.literal: If he hears that the forbidden army is being separately dispatched, the general will shrink back and not dare take responsibility—the bandits' outcome would be unknowable."
translations.idiomatic: If he learns we're sending a separate imperial force, he'll pull back and refuse command—and the rebels' fate becomes unpredictable."

sentences.zh: 」時惟商輅然其言。

translations.literal: " At the time only Shang Lu agreed with his words.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shang Lu agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 至冬，賊果平，人乃大服。

translations.literal: When winter came, the bandits were indeed pacified, and people greatly submitted in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: By winter the rebels were indeed crushed, and everyone came to admire Shi's judgment.

sentences.zh: 改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 五年得疾在告。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he fell ill and took leave on report.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he fell ill and asked for sick leave.

sentences.zh: 逾三月，帝趣赴閣視事，免朝參。

translations.literal: After more than three months, the Emperor pressed him to come to the Grand Secretariat to attend to affairs, exempting him from court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: After three months the Emperor summoned him back to the Grand Secretariat, exempting him from attending court.

sentences.zh: 是冬，無雪。

translations.literal: That winter there was no snow.
translations.idiomatic: That winter brought no snow.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「光祿寺采辦，各城門抽分，掊克不堪。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "The Guanglu Temple's procurement, with apportionment at each city gate, squeezes and oppresses unbearably.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The Guanglu Temple's procurement, with levies at every city gate, has become extortion beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 而獻珍珠寶石者，倍估增直，漁竭帑藏。

translations.literal: While those presenting pearls and precious stones double the appraisal and raise prices, they fish out and drain the treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: Those offering pearls and gems inflate valuations and bleed the treasury dry.

sentences.zh: 乞革其弊，以惠小民。

translations.literal: I beg to abolish these abuses, to benefit the common people.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that these abuses be abolished for the people's sake.

sentences.zh: 」帝優詔褒納。

translations.literal: " The Emperor with gracious edict praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor responded with a gracious edict of praise and acceptance.

sentences.zh: 畿輔、山東、河南旱，請免夏稅鹽鈔，及太仆寺賠課馬。

translations.literal: The capital region, Shandong, and Henan suffered drought; he requested exemption of summer taxes and salt certificates, and of the Taipusi Temple's compensatory duty horses.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck the capital region, Shandong, and Henan, he asked to waive summer taxes and salt certificates, and the Taipusi's compensatory horse quotas.

sentences.zh: 京師米貴，請發倉儲五十萬石平糶。

translations.literal: With capital rice expensive, he requested issuing five hundred thousand piculs from storehouses for sale at fair price.
translations.idiomatic: With grain prices soaring in the capital, he asked to release five hundred thousand piculs from granaries for sale at fair price.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were granted.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 時以舊臣見倚重，遇事爭執無所避。

translations.literal: Shi as an old minister was seen as relied upon and heavy; when matters arose he disputed without avoiding anything.
translations.idiomatic: As a senior minister in whom the Emperor placed great trust, Shi held nothing back in debate when issues arose.

sentences.zh: 而是時帝怠於政，大臣希得見。

translations.literal: But at this time the Emperor was negligent toward governance, and great ministers rarely got to see him.
translations.idiomatic: But the Emperor had grown negligent of government affairs, and senior ministers rarely gained audience.

sentences.zh: 萬安同在閣，結中貴戚畹，上下壅隔，時頗懷憂。

translations.literal: Wan An was in the Grand Secretariat together with him, bonding with middle-ranking esteemed relatives by marriage; upper and lower were blocked and separated, and Shi was somewhat worried.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An sat in the Grand Secretariat with him, cultivating ties with powerful eunuchs and imperial in-laws—court and throne were cut off from each other, and Shi grew deeply concerned.

sentences.zh: 七年，疾復作，乞致仕。

translations.literal: In the seventh year his illness returned; he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year his illness returned and he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝慰留之，不得去。

translations.literal: The Emperor comforted him and kept him; he could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor urged him to stay and would not let him go.

sentences.zh: 冬，彗復見，時言政本七事：一，毋惑佛事，糜金錢；

translations.literal: In winter the comet appeared again; Shi spoke of seven fundamentals of governance: First, do not be deluded by Buddhist affairs, wasting gold and money;
translations.idiomatic: When the comet reappeared that winter, Shi set out seven principles of good government: First, do not be seduced by Buddhist rites that squander gold and silver;

sentences.zh: 二，傳旨專委司禮監，毋令他人，以防詐偽；

translations.literal: Second, transmit edicts exclusively entrusted to the Directorate of Ceremonial, not allowing others, to guard against fraud and falsity;
translations.idiomatic: Second, route imperial orders exclusively through the Directorate of Ceremonial, not through others, to prevent forgery;

sentences.zh: 三，延見大臣議政事；

translations.literal: Third, extend audience to great ministers to deliberate on state affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Third, receive senior ministers to deliberate on state affairs;

sentences.zh: 四，近幸賜予太多，工匠冒官無紀，而重囚死徙者，法不蔽罪。

translations.literal: Fourth, favorites receive too many grants; artisans falsely claim office without discipline, while those in heavy punishment of death or exile—law does not cover the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, favorites receive too many gifts; artisans hold fake offices with no oversight, while convicted felons escape proper punishment;

sentences.zh: 宜戒淫刑僭賞；

translations.literal: One should guard against excessive punishments and usurping rewards;
translations.idiomatic: restrain excessive punishments and improper rewards;

sentences.zh: 五，虛懷受諫，勿惡切直；

translations.literal: Fifth, with empty breast receive remonstrance; do not hate blunt forthrightness;
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, welcome remonstrance with an open mind; do not resent blunt counsel;

sentences.zh: 六，戒廷臣毋依違，凡政令失當，直言論奏；

translations.literal: Sixth, admonish court ministers not to vacillate; whenever policies and orders are improper, speak frankly in memorial and presentation;
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, warn court officials against vacillation—whenever policy goes wrong, speak up directly;

sentences.zh: 七，清理牧馬草地，減退勢要莊田。

translations.literal: Seventh, clear and sort horse pasture lands, reduce and return powerful persons' estate fields.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, reclaim pasturelands and reduce the estates of the powerful.

sentences.zh: 皆切中時弊。

translations.literal: All cut directly to the abuses of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Every point struck at the day's ills.

sentences.zh: 寧晉伯劉聚為從父太監永誠請封謚，且乞祠額，禮部執故事卻之。

translations.literal: Marquis of Ningjin Liu Ju requested posthumous enfeoffment and title for his father's younger brother the eunuch Yong Cheng, and also begged a shrine inscription; the Ministry of Rites upheld precedent and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Ningjin Liu Ju petitioned for enfeoffment and a posthumous title for his uncle, the eunuch Yong Cheng, and also requested a shrine inscription—the Ministry of Rites invoked precedent and refused.

sentences.zh: 帝特賜額曰「褒功」，命內閣擬封謚。

translations.literal: The Emperor specially granted an inscription reading "Commending Merit" and ordered the Grand Secretariat to draft enfeoffment and posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally granted the inscription "Commending Merit" and ordered the Grand Secretariat to draft enfeoffment and a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 時等言：「即予永誠，將來守邊內臣皆援此陳乞，是變祖宗法自今日始。

translations.literal: Shi and others said: "If we grant this to Yong Cheng, in future border-guarding inner officials will all cite this in petition—the alteration of ancestral law would begin from today."
translations.idiomatic: Shi and his colleagues argued, "Grant this to Yong Cheng and every border eunuch will cite it as precedent—we would be changing ancestral law starting today."

sentences.zh: 」或言宋童貫封王，時曰：「貫封王在徽宗末年，豈盛世事耶？

translations.literal: " Someone spoke of Song Tong Guan being enfeoffed as king; Shi said: "Guan's enfeoffment as king was in the final years of Emperor Huizong—how could that be an affair of a flourishing age?"
translations.idiomatic: " Someone cited Tong Guan's enfeoffment as king in the Song. Shi replied, "That was in Huizong's last years—hardly a model for a golden age, is it?"

sentences.zh: 」乃寢。

translations.literal: " Thus the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時每因災變上言，或留中，或下所司，多阻隔，悒悒不得誌。

translations.literal: Shi often because of calamities and anomalies sent up words; sometimes they were kept within, sometimes sent down to the responsible offices—mostly blocked and obstructed; depressed, he could not achieve his aim.
translations.idiomatic: Shi often memorialized when disasters struck, but his submissions were held back or diverted—with little effect—and he grew depressed, unable to achieve what he sought.

sentences.zh: 五年以後，凡七在告，帝輒命醫就視，數遣內臣賜賚。

translations.literal: After the fifth year, on seven occasions of leave on report in total, the Emperor each time ordered physicians to visit and examine, repeatedly dispatching inner officials with gifts and bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: After the fifth year he took sick leave seven times, and each time the Emperor sent physicians and eunuchs bearing gifts.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，以秩滿進少保。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, on completion of tenure he was promoted to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year, his tenure complete, he was promoted to Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 逾月卒，年六十。

translations.literal: After a month he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he died, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚文憲。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor, posthumous name Wénxiàn.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 時立朝三十年，孜孜奉國，持正存大體，公退未嘗以政語子弟。

translations.literal: Shi stood at court thirty years, diligently serving the state, upholding rectitude and preserving the great frame; after returning from public duty he never spoke of government affairs to sons and younger kin.
translations.idiomatic: Shi served at court for thirty years, devoted to the state, upright and mindful of the larger good—after work he never discussed politics with his family.

sentences.zh: 有所論薦，不使其人知。

translations.literal: When he had someone to recommend in discussion, he did not let that person know.
translations.idiomatic: When he recommended someone, he never told them.

sentences.zh: 燕居無惰容，服禦儉約，無聲樂之奉，非其義不取，有古大臣風。

translations.literal: At ease in leisure he had no slack countenance; his dress and use were frugal and economical, with no music and song for enjoyment; what was not righteous he did not take—he had the bearing of an ancient great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Even at home he kept a disciplined bearing; he dressed plainly, kept no musicians, took nothing unearned—he had the bearing of the great ministers of old.

sentences.zh: 三年，錦衣指揮盧忠令校尉上變，告上皇與少監阮浪、內使王瑤圖復位。

translations.literal: In the third year, Brocade Guard commander Lu Zhong ordered a bailiff to submit an extraordinary report, reporting that the Retired Emperor and Junior Supervisor Ruan Lang and Inner Attendant Wang Yao plotted restoration.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Brocade Guard commander Lu Zhong had an officer submit an urgent report accusing the Retired Emperor, Junior Supervisor Ruan Lang, and Inner Attendant Wang Yao of plotting restoration.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，捕二人下詔獄，窮治之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was shaken with rage, arrested the two men and sent them to the imperial prison, thoroughly investigating them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage, arrested the two men, and had them tortured in the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 忠筮於術者同寅，寅以大義折之，且曰：「此大兇兆，死不足贖。

translations.literal: Zhong divined with the technician Tong Yin; Yin refuted him with great principle and also said: "This is a great ominous portent—death would not suffice for atonement."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong consulted the diviner Tong Yin, who rebuked him on moral grounds: "This is an evil omen—death wouldn't atone for it."

sentences.zh: 」忠懼，佯狂以冀免。

translations.literal: " Zhong was afraid and feigned madness hoping to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zhong feigned madness hoping to escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 輅及中官王誠言於帝曰：「忠病風，無足信，不宜聽妄言，傷大倫。

translations.literal: Lu and the inner official Wang Cheng spoke to the Emperor: "Zhong is sick with wind, not worth trusting—one should not listen to reckless words and harm the great human bonds."
translations.idiomatic: Lu and eunuch Wang Cheng told the Emperor, "Zhong is mad with illness—he's not credible. Don't heed this slander and violate the bonds of kinship."

sentences.zh: 」帝意少解。

translations.literal: " The Emperor's intent somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's anger subsided somewhat.

sentences.zh: 乃並下忠獄，坐以他罪，降為事官立功。

translations.literal: Then Zhong too was sent to prison, convicted on other crimes, demoted to a service official to perform meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was also imprisoned, convicted on other charges, and demoted to serve as a common soldier to earn redemption.

sentences.zh: 殺瑤，錮浪於獄，事得不竟。

translations.literal: Yao was killed; Lang was imprisoned in the jail; the affair accordingly did not reach completion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yao was executed and Ruan Lang imprisoned—the plot was never fully pursued.

sentences.zh: 太子既易，進兵部左侍郎，兼左春坊大學士如故，賜第南薰裏。

translations.literal: Once the Crown Prince was changed, he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of War, continuing as before Left Chunfang Grand Academician, and granted a residence in Nanxun Lane.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince was replaced, he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of War while retaining his post as Left Chunfang Grand Academician, and given a residence in Nanxun Lane.

sentences.zh: 塞上腴田率為勢豪侵據，輅請核還之軍。

translations.literal: Fertile fields on the frontier were generally encroached and occupied by powerful magnates; Lu requested verification and return of them to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Fertile frontier lands had been seized by the powerful; Lu requested they be surveyed and restored to military use.

sentences.zh: 開封、鳳陽諸府饑民流濟寧、臨清間，為有司驅逐。

translations.literal: Starving people from Kaifeng, Fengyang, and other prefectures drifted between Jining and Linqing, and were driven off by local officials.
translations.idiomatic: Starving refugees from Kaifeng and Fengyang drifted toward Jining and Linqing, only to be driven away by local officials.

sentences.zh: 輅憂其為變，請招墾畿內八府閑田，給糧種，民皆有所歸。

translations.literal: Lu feared they would turn to rebellion; he requested recruiting cultivation of idle fields in the eight prefectures within the capital region, providing grain and seed—the people all had somewhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing unrest, Lu proposed resettling them on idle land in eight prefectures near the capital with seed grain—giving the refugees a place to settle.

sentences.zh: 鐘同、章綸下獄，輅力救得無死。

translations.literal: Zhong Tong and Zhang Lun were sent to prison; Lu vigorously rescued them so they did not die.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Tong and Zhang Lun were imprisoned, Lu fought to save them from execution.

sentences.zh: 《寰宇通志》成，加兼太常卿。

translations.literal: When the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm was completed, he was additionally appointed Concurrent Grand Minister of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: When the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Realm was completed, he was additionally made Grand Minister of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 景帝不豫，群臣請建東宮，不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing was unwell; the ministers requested establishing an Eastern Palace; he did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing fell ill, ministers petitioned to name a crown prince—the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 將繼奏，輅援筆曰：「陛下宣宗章皇帝之子，當立章皇帝子孫。

translations.literal: About to continue the memorial, Lu took up the brush and wrote: "Your Majesty is the son of Emperor Xuanzong and Emperor Zhang; you should establish Emperor Zhang's sons and descendants."
translations.idiomatic: As the memorial continued, Lu wrote: "Your Majesty is the son of Emperor Xuan and Emperor Zhang—you should name a descendant of Emperor Zhang as heir."

sentences.zh: 」聞者感動。

translations.literal: " Those who heard were moved.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it were moved.

sentences.zh: 以日暮，奏未入，而是夜石亨輩已迎復上皇。

translations.literal: Because dusk fell, the memorial had not been submitted—and that very night Shi Heng and his faction already welcomed back the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk came before the memorial could be submitted—and that very night Shi Heng and his faction restored the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 明日，王文、于謙等被收，召輅與高谷入便殿，溫旨諭之，命草復位詔。

translations.literal: The next day Wang Wen, Yu Qian, and others were arrested; Lu and Gao Gu were summoned to the side hall, given warm edict and instruction, and ordered to draft the restoration edict.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wang Wen and Yu Qian were arrested. Lu and Gao Gu were summoned to the side hall, addressed with gentle words, and ordered to draft the restoration edict.

sentences.zh: 亨密語輅，赦文毋別具條款。

translations.literal: Heng privately told Lu that the amnesty document should not separately set forth special articles.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng privately told Lu that the amnesty should not list separate charges.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「舊制也，不敢易。

translations.literal: Lu said: "That is old regulation—I dare not alter it."
translations.idiomatic: Lu replied, "That is established practice—I dare not change it."

sentences.zh: 」亨輩不悅，諷言官劾輅朋奸，下之獄。

translations.literal: " Heng and his faction were displeased; they incited censorial officials to impeach Lu for factional treachery, and he was sent down to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng's faction was displeased and had censors impeach Lu for complicity; he was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 輅上書自訴《復儲疏》在禮部，可覆驗，不省。

translations.literal: Lu submitted a memorial in self-defense: his Memorial on Restoring the Heir was in the Ministry of Rites and could be re-verified—this was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Lu petitioned in his defense, noting that his Memorial on Restoring the Heir was on file at the Ministry of Rites and could be verified—the court ignored him.

sentences.zh: 中官興安稍解之，帝愈怒。

translations.literal: The inner official Xing An tried to intercede for him, but the Emperor grew even angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Xing An tried to intercede for him, but the Emperor only grew angrier.

sentences.zh: 安曰：「向者此輩創議南遷，不審置陛下何地。

translations.literal: An said: "Formerly these people first proposed moving south—without considering where to place Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Xing An said, "These same men once proposed retreating south—did they ever consider where that would leave Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 」帝意漸釋，乃斥為民。

translations.literal: " The Emperor's intent gradually released; Lu was then dismissed as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's anger gradually eased, and Lu was banished to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 然帝每獨念「輅，朕所取士，嘗與姚夔侍東宮」，不忍棄之。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor often alone recalled, "Lu—he is a scholar I personally selected, who once with Yao Kui attended the Eastern Palace," and could not bear to abandon him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Emperor often thought to himself, "Lu is a scholar I chose myself—he once served the Eastern Palace with Yao Kui," and could not bring himself to discard him entirely.

sentences.zh: 以忌者，竟不復用。

translations.literal: Because of those who envied him, in the end he was never again employed.
translations.idiomatic: But enemies blocked his recall, and he was never reappointed.

sentences.zh: 明年，彗星見，給事中董旻、御史胡深等劾不職大臣，並及輅。

translations.literal: The next year a comet appeared; Supervising Secretary Dong Min, Censor Hu Shen, and others impeached incompetent great ministers, reaching Lu as well.
translations.idiomatic: The next year a comet appeared, and supervising secretary Dong Min and censor Hu Shen impeached negligent ministers—including Lu.

sentences.zh: 御史林誠詆輅曾與易儲，不宜用，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Censor Lin Cheng slandered Lu as having once participated in changing the heir—unfit for employment; the Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lin Cheng attacked Lu for his role in the succession crisis and argued he should not be used—the Emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 輅因求罷。

translations.literal: Lu thereupon requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Lu then asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命廷鞫諸言者，欲加重譴。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and ordered court interrogation of all who had spoken, intending to impose heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angered and ordered a public trial of the accusers, intending harsh punishment.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「臣嘗請優容言者，今論臣反責之，如公論何？

translations.literal: Lu said: "Your subject once requested lenient treatment for those who speak; now concerning my case you instead blame them—what of public opinion?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu said, "I have pleaded for tolerance toward critics—yet now you would punish them for attacking me. What would people think?"

sentences.zh: 」帝悅，旻等各予杖復職。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was pleased; Min and the others each received beating and were restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased; Dong Min and the others were beaten but kept their posts.

sentences.zh: 尋進兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 久之，進戶部。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was promoted to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 《宋元通鑒綱目》成，改兼文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: When the Outline General History of Song and Yuan was completed, he was changed to concurrent Grand Academician of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Outline General History of Song and Yuan was completed, he became concurrent Grand Academician of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 皇太子立，加太子少保，進吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was established, he was added as Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince and promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was established, he was made Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince and promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十三年進謹身殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Grand Academician of the Jinshen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteenth year brought his promotion to Grand Academician of the Jinshen Hall.

sentences.zh: 輅為人，平粹簡重，寬厚有容，至臨大事，決大議，毅然莫能奪。

translations.literal: Lu as a person was even and pure, simple and grave, broad and generous with forbearance; yet facing great affairs and deciding great deliberations, he was resolute and none could sway him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was even-tempered, dignified, and generous by nature—yet when great affairs were at stake he was resolute and immovable.

sentences.zh: 仁壽太后莊戶與民爭田，帝欲徙民塞外。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Renshou's estate tenants disputed fields with commoners; the Emperor wished to relocate the people beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When tenants of Empress Dowager Renshou's estates disputed land with commoners, the Emperor proposed resettling the peasants beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「天子以天下為家，安用皇莊為？

translations.literal: Lu said: "The Son of Heaven takes all under Heaven as his home—of what use are imperial estates?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu said, "The Emperor's domain is all under Heaven—why does he need private royal estates?"

sentences.zh: 」事遂寢。

translations.literal: " The affair accordingly was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 乾清宮門災，工部請采木川、湖。

translations.literal: When the Qianqing Palace gate suffered fire, the Ministry of Works requested timber procurement from Sichuan and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After fire destroyed the Qianqing Palace gate, the Ministry of Works requested timber from Sichuan and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 輅言宜少緩，以存警畏，從之。

translations.literal: Lu said it was fitting to slow slightly, to preserve vigilance and awe; this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu urged delay to preserve a sense of caution—the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 悼恭太子薨，帝以繼嗣為憂。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Daogong died, the Emperor was anxious about succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Daogong died, the Emperor despaired over the succession.

sentences.zh: 紀妃生皇子，六歲矣，左右畏萬貴妃，莫敢言。

translations.literal: Consort Ji had borne a prince, already six years old; those around feared Consort Wan and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Ji had borne a prince, now six years old, but those around feared Consort Wan and none dared tell the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃聞於帝。

translations.literal: After a long time, it finally reached the Emperor's ears.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually the secret reached the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，欲宣示外廷，遣中官至內閣諭意。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly rejoiced and wished to announce it to the outer court; he dispatched an inner official to the Grand Secretariat to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was overjoyed and wanted to announce it publicly; he sent a eunuch to the Grand Secretariat with his wishes.

sentences.zh: 輅請敕禮部擬上皇子名，於是廷臣相率稱賀。

translations.literal: Lu requested an edict ordering the Ministry of Rites to draft and present the prince's name; thus court ministers one after another offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Lu asked that the Ministry of Rites be commanded to propose a name for the prince—and court officials lined up to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 帝即命皇子出見廷臣。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately ordered the prince to come out and meet the court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor immediately had the prince presented to the court.

sentences.zh: 越數日，帝復禦文華殿，皇子侍，召見輅及諸閣臣。

translations.literal: After several days, the Emperor again held audience at the Wenhua Hall with the prince in attendance, summoning Lu and the various Grand Secretaries for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the Emperor held court at the Wenhua Hall with the prince beside him and summoned Lu and the other grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 輅頓首曰：「陛下踐祚十年，儲副未立，天下引領望久矣。

translations.literal: Lu kowtowed and said: "Your Majesty has ascended the throne ten years; the heir deputy has not been established—the realm has long craned its neck in hope."
translations.idiomatic: Lu kowtowed and said, "Your Majesty has reigned ten years without an heir—the whole realm has waited with bated breath."

sentences.zh: 當即立為皇太子，安中外心。

translations.literal: He should immediately be established as Crown Prince, to settle hearts within and without."
translations.idiomatic: Name him crown prince at once—put court and country at ease."

sentences.zh: 」帝頷之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor nodded in agreement.

sentences.zh: 是冬，遂立皇子為皇太子。

translations.literal: That winter the prince was accordingly established as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the prince was formally named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，帝召見皇子留宮中，而紀妃仍居西內。

translations.literal: At first, the Emperor summoned the prince for audience and kept him in the palace, while Consort Ji still resided in the Western Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor had the prince brought to court and kept him in the palace, while Consort Ji remained in the western inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 輅恐有他患，難顯言，偕同官上疏曰：「皇子聰明岐嶷，國本攸系。

translations.literal: Lu feared some other misfortune and found it hard to speak openly; together with his colleagues he submitted a memorial saying: "The prince is bright and precocious—the foundation of the state depends on him."
translations.idiomatic: Lu feared other troubles were brewing and could not speak plainly; he and his colleagues submitted a memorial: "The prince is clever and quick-witted—the succession of the realm rests on him."

sentences.zh: 重以貴妃保護，恩逾己出。

translations.literal: Moreover, under the noble consort's protection, the favor shown him exceeds what one receives from one's own birth.
translations.idiomatic: Under the noble consort's care he has been shown kindness greater than a son receives from his own mother.

sentences.zh: 但外議謂皇子母因病別居，久不得見。

translations.literal: But outside opinion says the prince's mother lives apart due to illness and for long has been unable to see him.
translations.idiomatic: But rumor holds that the prince's mother, ill, has been kept apart and has not seen her son in a long time.

sentences.zh: 宜移就近所，俾母子朝夕相接，而皇子仍藉撫育於貴妃，宗社幸甚。

translations.literal: It is fitting to move her to a nearby residence, so that mother and son may meet morning and evening, while the prince still relies on the noble consort for nurturing—great fortune for altars and state.
translations.idiomatic: She should be moved to quarters nearby so mother and son may meet each day, while the prince continues to be raised under the noble consort—a blessing for throne and realm.

sentences.zh: 」由是紀妃遷永壽宮。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Consort Ji was moved to Yongshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On this advice Consort Ji was moved to Yongshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 逾月，妃病篤。

translations.literal: After more than a month, the consort's illness grew critical.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later the consort fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 輅請曰：「如有不諱，禮宜從厚。

translations.literal: Lu requested: "If the worst should come, rites ought to be carried out with full generosity."
translations.idiomatic: Lu asked that should the worst happen, she be accorded the fullest rites of mourning.

sentences.zh: 」且請命司禮監奉皇子，過妃宮問視，及制衰服行禮。

translations.literal: " He also requested that the Directorate of Ceremonial be ordered to escort the prince to pass by the consort's palace to inquire after her, and to prepare mourning garments and perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the Directorate of Ceremonial escort the prince to visit her at her palace and that mourning garments be made so the proper rites could be performed.

sentences.zh: 帝皆是之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed to all of this.

sentences.zh: 帝將復郕王位號，下廷議。

translations.literal: The Emperor intended to restore the princely title and rank of the Prince of Cheng and submitted the matter for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved to restore the Prince of Cheng's title and rank, he put the question to the court for discussion.

sentences.zh: 輅極言王有社稷功，位號當復，帝意遂決。

translations.literal: Lu spoke forcefully that the prince had merit for altars and state and his title and rank ought to be restored; the Emperor's intent was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lu argued at length that the prince had saved the realm and deserved restoration—the emperor's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 帝建玉皇閣於宮北，命內臣執事，禮與郊祀等，輅等爭罷之。

translations.literal: The Emperor built the Jade Emperor Pavilion north of the palace, ordered eunuchs to administer it, with rites equal to suburban sacrifices; Lu and others contended until it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had a Jade Emperor Pavilion built north of the palace, put eunuchs in charge, and gave its rites parity with the state sacrifices to Heaven—Lu and others protested until the project was scrapped.

sentences.zh: 黑眚見，疏弭災八事，曰：番僧國師法王，毋濫賜印章；

translations.literal: A dark plague-star appeared; he memorialized eight measures to avert calamity, saying: To Tibetan monks, national preceptors, and dharma kings—do not lavishly bestow seals;
translations.idiomatic: When a dark omen appeared in the sky, he submitted eight proposals to ward off disaster: do not hand out seals indiscriminately to Tibetan lamas, state preceptors, and dharma kings;

sentences.zh: 四方常貢外，勿受玩好；

translations.literal: Beyond the regular tribute from the four directions, do not accept curios and delights;
translations.idiomatic: accept no luxuries or curios beyond regular tribute from the provinces;

sentences.zh: 許諸臣直言；

translations.literal: Permit all ministers to speak forthrightly;
translations.idiomatic: let ministers speak their minds freely;

sentences.zh: 分遣部使慮囚，省冤獄；

translations.literal: Dispatch departmental envoys in separate missions to review prisoners, reducing wrongful imprisonment;
translations.idiomatic: send officials throughout the realm to review prisoners and clear wrongful convictions;

sentences.zh: 停不急營造，實三邊軍儲；

translations.literal: Halt non-urgent construction, filling the three-frontier military stores;
translations.idiomatic: halt nonessential construction and fill the border garrisons' granaries;

sentences.zh: 守沿邊關隘；

translations.literal: Guard the passes along the borders;
translations.idiomatic: strengthen defense of frontier passes;

sentences.zh: 設雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: Establish a Yunnan grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: establish a grand coordinator for Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔褒納。

translations.literal: The Emperor with an excellent edict praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with a gracious edict of praise and acceptance.

sentences.zh: 中官汪直之督西廠也，數興大獄。

translations.literal: When the eunuch Wang Zhi supervised the Western Depot, he repeatedly stirred up major cases.
translations.idiomatic: While the eunuch Wang Zhi ran the Western Depot, he repeatedly opened major prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 輅率同官條直十一罪，言：「陛下委聽斷於直，直又寄耳目於群小如韋瑛輩。

translations.literal: Lu led his colleagues in listing eleven crimes of Zhi, saying: "Your Majesty has entrusted hearing and judgment to Zhi, and Zhi in turn has lodged his eyes and ears in petty men such as Wei Ying and company."
translations.idiomatic: Lu led his colleagues in listing eleven charges against Zhi: "Your Majesty has left judgment to Zhi, and Zhi has put his spies in the hands of petty men like Wei Ying and his sort."

sentences.zh: 皆自言承密旨，得顓刑殺，擅作威福，賊虐善良。

translations.literal: All claim to receive secret edicts, obtaining exclusive power over punishment and killing, wielding authority and favor at will, and savaging the virtuous and good.
translations.idiomatic: They all claim secret imperial orders and wield the power of life and death, making arbitrary use of authority and tormenting the innocent.

sentences.zh: 陛下若謂擿奸禁亂，法不得已，則前此數年，何以帖然無事？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty holds that uncovering traitors and forbidding disorder makes such law unavoidable—then in the preceding several years, why was all quiet and without incident?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty believes uncovering traitors requires such measures, why were the preceding years peaceful and untroubled?

sentences.zh: 且曹欽之變，由逯杲刺事激成，可為懲鑒。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Calamity of Cao Qin was provoked and brought about by Su Gao's intelligence work—it may serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Qin rebellion was provoked by Su Gao's secret informants—a lesson that should not be forgotten.

sentences.zh: 自直用事，士大夫不安其職，商賈不安於途，庶民不安於業，若不亟去，天下安危未可知也。

translations.literal: Since Zhi came to power, scholar-officials have been uneasy in their posts, merchants uneasy on the roads, common people uneasy in their trades—if he is not quickly removed, the safety or danger of the realm cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhi took power, officials cannot do their work in peace, merchants travel in fear, and common folk cannot ply their trades in tranquility. If he is not removed soon, the realm's safety is in doubt.

sentences.zh: 」帝慍曰：「用一內豎，何遽危天下，誰主此奏者？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said angrily: "By employing one inner attendant, how could the realm suddenly be endangered? Who drafted this memorial?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped: "Because I employ one palace eunuch, the realm is suddenly in peril? Who wrote this memorial?"

sentences.zh: 」命太監懷恩傳旨，詰責厲甚。

translations.literal: " He ordered the eunuch Huai En to convey the imperial message, rebuking and criticizing with great severity.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the eunuch Huai En with an imperial message of stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 輅正色曰：「朝臣無大小，有罪皆請旨逮問，直擅抄沒三品以上京官。

translations.literal: Lu with stern countenance said: "Court ministers great and small—when guilty, all await imperial order before arrest and inquiry; Zhi on his own authority seizes and confiscates from capital officials of third rank and above."
translations.idiomatic: Lu answered firmly: "When any court official commits a crime, imperial approval is required before arrest. Zhi on his own authority seizes and plunders officials of third rank and above in the capital."

sentences.zh: 大同、宣府，邊城要害，守備俄頃不可缺。

translations.literal: Datong and Xuanfu—key border cities—cannot for an instant lack their garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Datong and Xuanfu are critical border fortresses whose commanders cannot be absent for a moment.

sentences.zh: 直一日械數人。

translations.literal: In one day Zhi fettered several men.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day Zhi put several of them in chains.

sentences.zh: 南京，祖宗根本地，留守大臣，直擅收捕。

translations.literal: Nanjing, the foundation-land of forefathers and ancestors—the resident minister there, Zhi on his own authority seized and arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing is the ancestral foundation of the dynasty, yet Zhi dares to arrest the resident minister there without authorization.

sentences.zh: 諸近侍在帝左右，直輒易置。

translations.literal: The various close attendants at the Emperor's side—Zhi readily displaces and replaces them.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants at Your Majesty's side—Zhi removes and replaces them at will.

sentences.zh: 直不去，天下安得無危？

translations.literal: If Zhi is not removed, how can the realm not be in danger?
translations.idiomatic: As long as Zhi remains, how can the realm be secure?

sentences.zh: 」萬安、劉珝、劉吉亦俱對，引義慷慨，恩等屈服。

translations.literal: " Wan An, Liu Xu, and Liu Ji also all responded, citing principle with ardor; En and the others submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wan An, Liu Xu, and Liu Ji spoke up as well, citing principle with passionate force; Huai En and the others backed down.

sentences.zh: 輅顧同列謝曰：「諸公皆為國如此，輅復何憂。

translations.literal: Lu turned to his colleagues and said in thanks: "You all have served the state thus—what further worry has Lu?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu turned to his colleagues and said: "With all of you serving the state with such courage, what have I to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」會九卿項忠等亦劾直，是日遂罷西廠。

translations.literal: " As it happened, the Nine Ministers including Xiang Zhong also impeached Zhi, and that day the Western Depot was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Nine Ministers led by Xiang Zhong also impeached Zhi, and the Western Depot was abolished.

sentences.zh: 直雖不視廠事，寵幸如故。

translations.literal: Though Zhi no longer oversaw depot affairs, his favor and grace remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhi no longer ran the depot, his imperial favor was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 譖輅嘗納指揮楊曄賄，欲脫其罪。

translations.literal: [Zhi] slandered Lu as having once accepted a bribe from Commander Yang Ye, wishing to escape his crime.
translations.idiomatic: He slandered Lu for having taken a bribe from Commander Yang Ye to secure his release.

sentences.zh: 輅不自安，而御史戴縉復頌直功，請復西廠，輅遂力求去。

translations.literal: Lu was ill at ease; then Censor Dai Jin again praised Zhi's merits and requested restoration of the Western Depot—Lu thereupon strove forcefully to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Lu grew uneasy, and when Censor Dai Jin praised Zhi and asked that the Western Depot be restored, Lu pressed hard to resign.

sentences.zh: 詔加少保，賜敕馳傳歸。

translations.literal: An edict added Junior Guardian and granted an imperial letter with post-horses for return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to junior guardian and sent home under imperial patent with post horses.

sentences.zh: 輅既去，士大夫益俯首事直，無敢與抗者矣。

translations.literal: Once Lu had departed, scholar-officials bent their heads even more in serving Zhi, with none daring to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu left, officials bowed even lower to Zhi, and none dared oppose him.

sentences.zh: 錢溥嘗以不遷官，作《禿婦傳》以譏輅。

translations.literal: Qian Pu, once for not receiving promotion, wrote "Biography of the Bald Wife" to ridicule Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Pu, passed over for promotion, once wrote "Biography of the Bald Wife" to mock Lu.

sentences.zh: 高瑤請復景帝位號，黎淳疏駁，極詆輅。

translations.literal: Gao Yao requested restoration of Emperor Jing's title and rank; Li Chun in a memorial refuted it, bitterly reviling Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yao petitioned to restore Emperor Jing's title, Li Chun wrote a rebuttal that fiercely attacked Lu.

sentences.zh: 輅皆不為較，待之如平時。

translations.literal: Lu in all cases did not contend, treating them as in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Lu took no offense and treated them as he always had.

sentences.zh: 萬貴妃重輅名，出父像，屬為贊，遺金帛甚厚。

translations.literal: Consort Wan honored Lu's reputation; she produced a portrait of her father, commissioning him to write an encomium, leaving gold and silks very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wan, who respected Lu's standing, sent a portrait of her father and asked him to write an encomium, along with generous gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 輅力辭，使者告以妃意。

translations.literal: Lu forcefully declined; the envoy conveyed the consort's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu firmly declined; the emissary relayed the consort's wishes.

sentences.zh: 輅曰：「非上命，不敢承也。

translations.literal: Lu said: "Without imperial command, I dare not accept."
translations.idiomatic: Lu said: "Without the emperor's order I dare not accept."

sentences.zh: 」貴妃不悅，輅終不顧。

translations.literal: " The noble consort was displeased; Lu to the end paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was displeased, but Lu held firm and ignored it.

sentences.zh: 其和而有執如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he harmonious yet principled.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his easy manner and unyielding principle.

sentences.zh: 及謝政，劉吉過之，見其子孫林立，嘆曰：「吉與公同事歷年，未嘗見公筆下妄殺一人，宜天之報公厚。

translations.literal: When he had retired from office, Liu Ji visited him, saw his sons and grandsons standing in ranks, and sighed: "Ji and you served together many years—I never saw you under your brush capriciously kill a single person; Heaven's reward to you is fittingly generous."
translations.idiomatic: After he retired, Liu Ji came to visit and saw his sons and grandsons gathered all around. Liu sighed: "In all our years together I never saw you sign an order for an innocent man's death. Heaven has been generous in its reward."

sentences.zh: 」輅曰：「正不敢使朝廷妄殺一人耳。

translations.literal: " Lu said: "It was precisely that I dared not let the court capriciously kill a single person."
translations.idiomatic: Lu replied: "I simply would not let the court put an innocent man to death."

sentences.zh: 」居十年卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: " He lived in retirement ten years and died, age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for ten years and died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚文毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Tutor and honored with the posthumous name Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand tutor with the posthumous name Wenyi ("Steadfast in Culture").

sentences.zh: 子良臣，成化初進士，官翰林侍講。

translations.literal: His son Liangchen, a jinshi of the early Chenghua reign, served as Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liangchen passed the jinshi examination in the early Chenghua era and served as a Hanlin reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 劉定之，字主靜，永新人。

translations.literal: Liu Dingzhi, style Zhujing, was a native of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dingzhi, styled Zhujing, was a native of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 幼有異稟。

translations.literal: As a child he had an unusual endowment.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he showed extraordinary gifts.

sentences.zh: 父授之書，日誦數千言。

translations.literal: His father taught him the classics; daily he recited several thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: His father taught him to read, and each day he could recite several thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 不令作文，一日偶見所為《祀竈文》。

translations.literal: He was not allowed to compose essays; one day [the father] happened to see what he had written, "Rite to the Stove Spirit."
translations.idiomatic: His father had not yet let him write compositions, but one day he happened upon an essay the boy had written on worshipping the Kitchen God.

sentences.zh: 大異之。

translations.literal: [The father] was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: He was astonished.

sentences.zh: 舉正統元年會試第一，殿試及第，授編修。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong he came first in the metropolitan examination, passed the palace examination, and was appointed Compiler.
