translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the metropolitan examination in the first year of Zhengtong, passed the palace examination, and was made a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 京城大水，應詔陳十事，言：「號令宜出大公，裁以至正，不可茍且數易。

translations.literal: When the capital suffered great flooding, in response to an edict he presented ten matters, saying: "Commands ought to issue from the greater public good, cut with utmost rectitude—not be hastily changed again and again."
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was flooded, he responded to an imperial call with ten proposals: "Edicts must serve the public good and be grounded in rectitude; they must not be issued carelessly or changed every other day."

sentences.zh: 公卿侍從，當數召見，察其才能心術而進退之。

translations.literal: Grand dukes, ministers, and attendants ought frequently to be summoned for audience, to observe their talent, ability, and character before promoting or demoting them.
translations.idiomatic: High ministers and court attendants should be summoned regularly so their talent and character can be judged before appointment or dismissal.

sentences.zh: 降人散處京畿者，宜漸移之南方。

translations.literal: Surrendered people scattered about the capital region ought gradually to be moved south.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered peoples scattered around the capital region should gradually be resettled in the south.

sentences.zh: 郡縣職以京朝官補，使叠相出入，內外無畸重。

translations.literal: Prefecture and county posts ought to be filled by capital court officials, so they pass in and out in succession, with neither inner nor outer unduly weighted.
translations.idiomatic: Prefecture and county posts should be filled by capital officials in rotation, so inner and outer service are balanced.

sentences.zh: 薦舉之法，不當拘五品以上。

translations.literal: The method of recommendation ought not to be restricted to fifth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: The recommendation system should not be limited to officials of fifth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 可仿唐制，朝臣遷秩，舉一人自代，吏部籍其名而簡用之。

translations.literal: It is feasible to model the Tang system: when court ministers transfer rank, each recommends one person to succeed himself, and the Ministry of Personnel registers the names and selects and employs them.
translations.idiomatic: We might follow the Tang practice: when a court official is promoted, he should nominate a successor, whose name the Ministry of Personnel records and considers for appointment.

sentences.zh: 武臣子孫，教以韜略。

translations.literal: The sons and grandsons of military ministers should be taught strategy and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of military families should be trained in strategy and tactics.

sentences.zh: 守令牧養為先務，毋徒取幹辦。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates should take nurturing the people as the first task—not merely select those skilled at execution.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials should be chosen for their ability to nurture the people, not merely for administrative efficiency.

sentences.zh: 群臣遭喪，乞永罷起復以教孝。

translations.literal: When ministers encounter mourning, I beg that return to office before mourning ends be permanently abolished, to teach filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Let the practice of "returning to duty" during mourning be permanently abolished, to teach filial piety.

sentences.zh: 僧尼蠹國當嚴絕。

translations.literal: Monks and nuns who plague the state ought to be strictly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Monks and nuns who drain the realm should be strictly curtailed.

sentences.zh: 富民輸粟授官者，有犯宜追奪。

translations.literal: Wealthy commoners who pay grain to receive office—if guilty, their titles ought to be pursued and revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who bought their ranks by donating grain should have those ranks revoked if they commit crimes.

sentences.zh: 」疏入留中。

translations.literal: " The memorial entered and was retained at court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received but shelved without action.

sentences.zh: 十三年，弟寅之與鄉人相訐，辭連定之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, his younger brother Yinzi quarreled with a fellow townsman; the words implicated Dingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year his younger brother Yinzi got into a dispute with a neighbor, and Dingzhi was implicated in the case.

sentences.zh: 下獄，得白。

translations.literal: [He] was imprisoned and cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He was thrown in prison but exonerated.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，進侍講。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，復上言十事，曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing ascended the throne, he again submitted ten statements, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing came to the throne, he submitted ten further proposals:

sentences.zh: 自古如晉懷、湣、宋徽、欽，皆因邊塞外破，藩鎮內潰，救援不集，馴致播遷。

translations.literal: From antiquity, such as Jin Huai and Min, Song Hui and Qin—all because the outer frontier was broken, inner frontier commands collapsed within, relief did not gather, and gradually they were driven to wandering exile.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors such as Jin Huai and Min, Song Huizong and Qinzong—all lost their thrones because the frontiers collapsed, inner garrisons disintegrated, and help never came, until they were driven into exile.

sentences.zh: 未有若今日以天下之大，數十萬之師，奉上皇於漠北，委以與寇者也。

translations.literal: Never has there been like today—with a realm so vast, an army of several hundred thousand, presenting the retired emperor in the northern deserts and entrusting him to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Never has there been a case like today—a vast empire and an army of hundreds of thousands, yet the former emperor was left in the northern desert and delivered into the enemy's hands.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋遭禍亂，棄故土，偏安一隅，尚能奮於既衰，以禦方張之敵。

translations.literal: Jin and Song, encountering calamity and disorder, abandoned their old lands and held to one corner in partial security—yet could still rouse themselves after decline to resist enemies in full expansion.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin and Song dynasties, even after losing their heartlands and retreating to partial rule, could still rally from weakness to face rising enemies.

sentences.zh: 未有若今日也先乘勝直抵都城。

translations.literal: Never has there been like today, when Esen riding victory pressed straight to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Never has an enemy like Esen, riding the momentum of victory, marched straight on the capital.

sentences.zh: 以師武臣之眾，既不能奮武以破賊，又不能約和以迎駕。

translations.literal: With troops so numerous and military ministers so many—they could neither exert martial force to break the bandits, nor make peace to welcome back the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: With vast armies and seasoned commanders, you could neither fight to defeat the enemy nor negotiate to bring the emperor home.

sentences.zh: 聽其自來而自去者也。

translations.literal: They only listened as the enemy came of themselves and departed of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: You simply let the enemy come and go as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 國勢之弱，雖非旦夕所能強，豈可不思自強之術而力行之。

translations.literal: The state's strength being weak—though it cannot be fortified in a morning and evening—can one fail to think on methods of self-strengthening and forcefully carry them out?
translations.idiomatic: The realm's weakness cannot be cured overnight, but can we fail to seek and vigorously pursue ways to strengthen it?

sentences.zh: 臣愚敢略陳所見。

translations.literal: Your minister, though dull, ventures briefly to set forth what he has seen.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant ventures to set forth what I see.

sentences.zh: 近日京軍之戰，但知堅壁持重，而不能用奇制勝。

translations.literal: In recent battles of the capital armies, they knew only to hold walls and maintain weight, but could not use surprise to achieve victory.
translations.idiomatic: In recent battles the capital troops knew only to hold firm behind walls and could not use surprise to win.

sentences.zh: 至前敗而後不救，左出而右不隨。

translations.literal: As for the front being defeated while the rear does not rescue, the left moving out while the right does not follow—
translations.idiomatic: When one unit is routed the rest do not come to its aid; when one flank advances the other does not follow.

sentences.zh: 謂宜仿宋吳玠、吳璘三疊陣法，互相倚恃，叠為救護。

translations.literal: [He] said it was fitting to model the Song generals Wu Jie and Wu Lin's triple-layered formation method, mutually relying on one another, layered for mutual rescue.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed adopting the triple-layer formation of the Song generals Wu Jie and Wu Lin, with units mutually supporting and covering one another.

sentences.zh: 至鐵騎沖突，必資刀斧以制之。

translations.literal: As for iron cavalry charging, one must rely on halberds and axes to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Against cavalry charges, halberds and axes are essential.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀破安祿山八萬騎，用千人執長刀如墻而進。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi broke An Lushan's eighty thousand riders, using a thousand men wielding long blades advancing like a wall.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi defeated An Lushan's eighty thousand horsemen with a thousand men advancing behind a wall of long blades.

sentences.zh: 韓世忠破兀术拐子馬，用五百人執長斧，上揕人胸，下斫馬足。

translations.literal: Han Shizhong broke Wuzhu's "guai zi" horses, using five hundred men wielding long axes—striking up to pierce men's chests, striking down to hack horse legs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong broke Wuzhu's linked cavalry with five hundred men wielding long axes, thrusting at riders' chests and chopping at horses' legs.

sentences.zh: 是刀斧揮霍便捷，優於火槍也。

translations.literal: Thus blade and axe, swung broadly with swift convenience, are superior to fire-guns.
translations.idiomatic: Blades and axes, wielded swiftly at close range, are more effective than firearms.

sentences.zh: 紫荊、居庸二關，名為關塞，實則坦途。

translations.literal: The two passes Zijing and Juyong—named border fortresses, but in truth level roads.
translations.idiomatic: The Zijing and Juyong passes are called fortresses, but in truth they are open highways.

sentences.zh: 今宜增兵士，繕亭障，塞蹊隧。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to increase soldiers, repair pavilion barriers, and block footpaths and tunnels.
translations.idiomatic: More troops should be posted there, watchtowers repaired, and hidden paths blocked.

sentences.zh: 陸則縱橫掘塹，名曰「地網」。

translations.literal: On land, dig trenches crisscross, called "Earth Net."
translations.idiomatic: On land, crisscrossing trenches should be dug—the "Earth Net."

sentences.zh: 水則氵豬泉令深，名曰「水櫃」。

translations.literal: In water, make the retention springs deep, called "Water Chest."
translations.idiomatic: In waterways, deepen the holding pools—the "Water Chest."

sentences.zh: 或多植榆柳，以制奔突，或多招鄉勇，以助官軍。

translations.literal: Or plant many elms and willows to check sudden rushes, or recruit many local braves to assist the official armies.
translations.idiomatic: Plant elm and willow barriers to check cavalry charges, and recruit local militia to support the regular troops.

sentences.zh: 此皆古所嘗為，已有明效。

translations.literal: These are all things anciently attempted, with clear effectiveness already proven.
translations.idiomatic: All these measures were used in antiquity and have proven effective.

sentences.zh: 往者奉使之臣，充以驛人駔夫，招釁啟戎，職此之故。

translations.literal: In the past, envoys on tribute missions were filled out with post-station men and horse-dealers, provoking quarrel and opening warfare—for this was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, tribute envoys were staffed with post-station runners and horse dealers—a practice that provoked border incidents and invited war.

sentences.zh: 今宜擇內蘊忠悃，外工專對，若陸賈、富弼其人者，使備正介之選，庶不失辭辱國。

translations.literal: Now one should select men who inwardly harbor loyal sincerity and outwardly excel at diplomatic replies—men like Lu Jia and Fu Bi—to stand ready as choices for chief envoys, so that the state may not suffer disgrace through ill-chosen words.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys should now be chosen for inner loyalty and outward skill in diplomacy—men in the mold of Lu Jia and Fu Bi—so that chief missions are never entrusted to speakers who would disgrace the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣於上皇朝，乞徙漠北降人，知謀短淺，未蒙采納。

translations.literal: Your subject, during the former emperor's reign, petitioned to relocate the surrendered people of the northern desert, knowing his counsel was shallow and short-sighted, yet it was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: During the former emperor's reign I had petitioned to resettle the surrendered tribes of the northern steppe; my plan was crude, and it was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 比乘國釁，奔歸故土，寇掠畿甸者屢見告矣。

translations.literal: Recently, taking advantage of the nation's crisis, they have fled back to their old lands, and reports of their raiding the capital region have come repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: They have since exploited the national crisis to return home, and raids on the capital region are reported again and again.

sentences.zh: 宜乘大兵聚集時，遷之南方。

translations.literal: It is fitting to take the occasion when great armies are assembled to relocate them to the south.
translations.idiomatic: While the main armies are still massed, they should be moved south.

sentences.zh: 使與中國兵民相錯雜，以牽制而變化之。

translations.literal: Have them intermixed with Chinese soldiers and civilians, so as to restrain and transform them.
translations.idiomatic: Intermingle them with Chinese troops and commoners so they can be controlled and gradually assimilated.

sentences.zh: 且可省俸給，減漕免，其事甚便。

translations.literal: Moreover, stipends may be saved and canal transport costs reduced—the affair would be very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: It would also save stipends and cut the cost of grain transport—a straightforward gain.

sentences.zh: 天下農出粟，女出布，以養兵也。

translations.literal: Under Heaven, farmers produce grain and women produce cloth to support the army.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers grow grain and women weave cloth to sustain the army.

sentences.zh: 兵受粟於倉，受布於庫，以衛國也。

translations.literal: Soldiers receive grain from the granary and cloth from the storehouse to defend the state.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers draw grain from the granaries and cloth from the storehouses in order to defend the realm.

sentences.zh: 向者兵士受粟布於公門，納月錢於私室。

translations.literal: Formerly soldiers received grain and cloth at the public gate but paid monthly fees in private quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers used to collect their grain and cloth at the public depot, then pay monthly fees into their officers' private coffers.

sentences.zh: 於是手不習擊刺之法，足不習進退之宜。

translations.literal: Thus their hands did not practice thrust-and-strike methods, nor their feet the proper arts of advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Their hands never learned thrust and parry; their feet never learned how to advance or withdraw in formation.

sentences.zh: 第轉貨為商，執技為工，而以工商所得，補納月錢。

translations.literal: They merely turned goods for trade as merchants and applied skills as craftsmen, using what commerce and craft earned to make up the monthly fees paid.
translations.idiomatic: They simply turned to trade and craft, using the profits to cover their monthly payments to their officers.

sentences.zh: 民之膏血，兵之氣力，皆變為金銀以惠奸宄。

translations.literal: The people's fat and blood, the soldiers' vital strength—all were transformed into gold and silver to benefit villains and wrongdoers.
translations.idiomatic: The people's sweat and the soldiers' strength were drained away as silver and gold into the pockets of corrupt men.

sentences.zh: 一旦率以臨敵，如驅羊拒狼，幾何其不敗也！

translations.literal: Once they are led to face the enemy, it is like driving sheep to resist wolves—how could they not be defeated!
translations.idiomatic: Lead such men against the enemy and it is like driving sheep before wolves—defeat is all but certain.

sentences.zh: 今宜痛革其弊，一新簡練之政，將帥踵舊習者誅毋赦。

translations.literal: Now one should sternly reform these abuses and wholly renew the policy of selection and training; generals who follow old corrupt practices should be executed without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: These abuses must be rooted out and training policy thoroughly reformed; any commander who clings to the old ways should be executed without mercy.

sentences.zh: 如是而兵威不振者，未之有也。

translations.literal: If this is done and military prestige is not revived, there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Do this, and the army's fighting spirit will surely be restored.

sentences.zh: 守令朘民，猶將帥之剝兵也。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates who squeeze the people are like generals who strip their soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When local officials bleed the people, it is no different from generals bleeding their troops.

sentences.zh: 宜嚴糾考，慎黜陟。

translations.literal: Strict investigation and assessment should be applied, and promotions and dismissals handled with care.
translations.idiomatic: Investigations should be rigorous and promotions and dismissals made with strict care.

sentences.zh: 犯贓者舉主與其罰，然後貪墨者寡，薦舉者慎，民安而邦本固矣。

translations.literal: For those who commit corruption, let their recommenders share the punishment; then the corrupt will be few, those who recommend will be cautious, the people secure, and the foundation of the state firm.
translations.idiomatic: When corrupt officials are punished together with those who recommended them, graft will dwindle, nominations will be made with caution, the people will be secure, and the state's foundations will hold firm.

sentences.zh: 古販繒屠狗之夫，俱足助成帝業。

translations.literal: In antiquity, men who sold silk and butchered dogs were all sufficient to help accomplish an imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, men who sold silk or butchered dogs could still help build an empire.

sentences.zh: 今于謙、楊善亦非出自將門。

translations.literal: Today Yu Qian and Yang Shan likewise did not come from military families.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian and Yang Shan today likewise did not come from military families.

sentences.zh: 然將能知將，宜令各舉所知，不限門閥。

translations.literal: Yet a general can recognize generals; each should be ordered to recommend those he knows, without limiting by family status.
translations.idiomatic: A good commander knows other good commanders; each should be asked to recommend men he knows, with no restriction by birth or clan.

sentences.zh: 公卿侍從，亦令舉勇力知謀之士，以備將材。

translations.literal: Dukes, ministers, and attendants should likewise be ordered to recommend men of courage, strength, and strategic knowledge, to supply general material.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and court attendants should likewise recommend men of courage, strength, and strategic talent to fill the ranks of command.

sentences.zh: 庶搜羅既廣，禦侮有人。

translations.literal: Thus, if the search is broad, there will be men to repel insult.
translations.idiomatic: Cast the net wide, and there will always be someone to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 昔者漢圖恢復，所恃者諸葛亮。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Han sought restoration, what it relied on was Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Han sought to recover its dominion, it relied on Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 南宋禦金，所恃者張浚。

translations.literal: The Southern Song in resisting Jin relied on Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Song, in resisting the Jin, relied on Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 彼皆忠義夙著，功業久立。

translations.literal: Both were long famed for loyalty and righteousness, with achievements established over many years.
translations.idiomatic: Both were men of long-proven loyalty whose achievements had stood the test of time.

sentences.zh: 及街亭一敗，亮辭丞相。

translations.literal: When Jieting fell in a single defeat, Liang resigned the post of Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Jieting, Liang resigned the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 符離未捷，浚解都督，何則？

translations.literal: When Fuli was not won, Jun was relieved of the post of Grand Marshal—why?
translations.idiomatic: When Fuli was not taken, Jun was stripped of his command as grand marshal—why?

sentences.zh: 賞罰明則將士奮也。

translations.literal: When rewards and punishments are clear, officers and soldiers are stirred to effort.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards and punishments are clear, officers and men fight with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 昨德勝門下之戰，未聞摧陷強寇，但叠為勝負，互殺傷而已。

translations.literal: In yesterday's battle below Desheng Gate, one did not hear of crushing and breaking the strong enemy—only alternating victories and defeats, mutual killing and wounding, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: In the recent battle at Desheng Gate, no decisive blow was struck against the enemy; the fighting merely seesawed back and forth with casualties on both sides.

sentences.zh: 雖不足罰，亦不足賞。

translations.literal: Though not sufficient for punishment, it was also not sufficient for reward.
translations.idiomatic: It merited neither punishment nor reward.

sentences.zh: 乃石亨則自伯進侯，于謙則自二品遷一品。

translations.literal: Yet Shi Heng was promoted from baron to marquis, and Yu Qian moved from second rank to first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shi Heng was raised from baron to marquis, and Yu Qian promoted from the second to the first rank.

sentences.zh: 天下未聞其功，但見其賞，豈不怠忠臣義士之心乎？

translations.literal: Under Heaven had not heard of their achievements, yet only saw their rewards—would this not slacken the hearts of loyal ministers and righteous warriors?
translations.idiomatic: The realm had heard nothing of their achievements, yet saw only their rewards—would that not dampen the zeal of loyal and righteous men?

sentences.zh: 可令仍循舊秩，勿躐新階，他日勛名著而爵賞加，正未為晚。

translations.literal: They may be ordered to keep their former ranks and not leap to new grades; when merit is famed on another day and titles and rewards are added, that will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Let them keep their former ranks for now rather than leap ahead; when their merit is truly established, titles and rewards can follow—and that will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 夫既與不忍奪者，姑息之政；

translations.literal: To grant what one cannot bear to take away is a policy of indulgence;
translations.idiomatic: To grant rewards one cannot bring oneself to revoke is indulgence;

sentences.zh: 既進不肯退者，患失之心。

translations.literal: To advance those who will not withdraw is the mind of fearing loss.
translations.idiomatic: To promote men who refuse to step back is the fear of losing what one holds.

sentences.zh: 上不行姑息之政，下不懷患失之心，則治平可計日而望也。

translations.literal: If above there is no policy of indulgence and below no mind of fearing loss, then good order and peace may be counted by days in prospect.
translations.idiomatic: If the throne rejects indulgence and officials shed their fear of loss, good government may be expected within days.

sentences.zh: 向者御史建白，欲令大臣入內議政，疏寢不行。

translations.literal: Formerly a censor memorialized, wishing to have great ministers enter the inner palace to discuss government; the memorial was shelved and not enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a censor proposed that senior ministers enter the inner court to deliberate on policy; the memorial was shelved and never carried out.

sentences.zh: 夫人主當總攬威權，親決機務。

translations.literal: The ruler ought to gather all authority to himself and personally decide critical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign should hold all authority in his own hands and decide critical affairs personally.

sentences.zh: 政事早朝未決者，日禦便殿，使大臣敷奏。

translations.literal: For government affairs undecided at the early audience, each day hold court in the side hall and have great ministers present and report.
translations.idiomatic: When morning audience leaves business unresolved, hold court daily in the side hall and have senior ministers present their views.

sentences.zh: 言官察其邪正而糾劾之，史官直書簡冊，以示懲勸。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials should examine their crookedness and uprightness and impeach them; historiographers should write directly in the registers, to show punishment and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Censors should scrutinize right and wrong and impeach where needed; historians should record the proceedings faithfully, so that reward and reproof are plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 此前代故事，祖宗成法也，願陛下遵而行之。

translations.literal: These are precedents of former ages and established laws of the ancestral house; I pray Your Majesty will follow and enact them.
translations.idiomatic: These are precedents of earlier dynasties and established practice of our own forebears; I pray Your Majesty will follow them.

sentences.zh: 若僅封章入奏，中旨外傳，恐偏聽獨任，致生奸亂，欲治化之成難矣。

translations.literal: If only sealed memorials are submitted and inner edicts transmitted outward, I fear partial listening and sole reliance will give rise to treachery and disorder, and the achievement of good rule and transformation will be hard.
translations.idiomatic: If governance consists only of sealed memorials going in and private edicts going out, partial counsel and unchecked power will breed corruption and disorder, and good government will be hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 人主之德，欲其明如日月以察直枉，仁如天地以覆群生，勇如雷霆以收威柄。

translations.literal: The virtue of a ruler should be bright as sun and moon to discern straight from crooked, benevolent as Heaven and Earth to cover all living beings, and bold as thunder to gather authority back to himself.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's virtue should be bright as the sun and moon to distinguish right from wrong, broad as Heaven and Earth in caring for the people, and fierce as thunder in reclaiming authority.

sentences.zh: 故司馬光之告君，以仁明武為言，即《中庸》所謂知仁勇也。

translations.literal: Thus when Sima Guang counseled his ruler, he spoke of benevolence, clarity, and martial resolve—what the Doctrine of the Mean calls wisdom, benevolence, and courage.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Guang counseled his ruler, he spoke of benevolence, clarity, and resolve—the wisdom, benevolence, and courage described in the Doctrine of the Mean.

sentences.zh: 知仁勇非學而能之哉？

translations.literal: Can wisdom, benevolence, and courage be attained without study?
translations.idiomatic: Can wisdom, benevolence, and courage be mastered without study?

sentences.zh: 夫經莫要於《尚書》、《春秋》，史莫正於《通鑒綱目》。

translations.literal: Among the classics, none is more essential than the Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals; among histories, none is more authoritative than the Comprehensive Mirror in Outline.
translations.idiomatic: Among the classics, none matters more than the Documents and the Spring and Autumn Annals; among histories, none is more authoritative than the Comprehensive Mirror in Outline.

sentences.zh: 陛下留心垂覽。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should attend to them and peruse them with care.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should read them with close attention.

sentences.zh: 其於君也，既知禹、湯、文、武之所以興，又知桀、紂、幽、厲之所以替，而趨避審矣。

translations.literal: In being a ruler, one will know both how Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu rose, and how Jie, Zhou, You, and Li fell—and one's course of pursuit and avoidance will be careful.
translations.idiomatic: As a ruler, one will learn both how Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu rose to power and how Jie, Zhou, You, and Li lost it—and one's choices will be the wiser for it.

sentences.zh: 於馭內臣也，既知有呂強、張承業之忠，又知有仇士良、陳弘誌之惡；

translations.literal: In governing inner attendants, one will know both the loyalty of Lü Qiang and Zhang Chengye and the wickedness of Qiu Shiliang and Chen Hongzhi;
translations.idiomatic: In managing inner attendants, one will know the loyalty of men like Lü Qiang and Zhang Chengye and the wickedness of men like Qiu Shiliang and Chen Hongzhi;

sentences.zh: 於馭廷臣也，既知有蕭、曹、房、杜之良，又知有李林甫、楊國忠之奸，而用舍當矣。

translations.literal: In governing court ministers, one will know both the worth of Xiao, Cao, Fang, and Du and the treachery of Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong—and employment and dismissal will be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: In managing court ministers, one will know the worth of men like Xiao He, Cao Can, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui and the treachery of men like Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong—and appointments will be made wisely.

sentences.zh: 如是則於知仁勇之德，豈不大有助哉。

translations.literal: If this is so, then for the virtue of wisdom, benevolence, and courage, would it not be of great help?
translations.idiomatic: In this way, would it not greatly strengthen the virtues of wisdom, benevolence, and courage?

sentences.zh: 茍徒如向者儒臣進講，誦述其善，諱避其惡，是猶恐道路之有陷阱，閉目而過之，其不至於冥行顛仆者幾何。

translations.literal: If one merely, like the Confucian ministers of before who lectured at court, recited their good points and avoided their evils, it would be like fearing traps in the road yet passing with eyes closed—how could one not eventually walk blindly and fall?
translations.idiomatic: If lectures merely recite the good and avoid the evil, as court scholars have done, it is like shutting one's eyes on a road full of pits—how long before one stumbles and falls?

sentences.zh: 今天下雖遭大創，尚如金甌之未缺。

translations.literal: Though the realm today has suffered a great wound, it is still like a golden bowl not yet broken.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm has suffered a grievous wound, it remains like a golden bowl not yet cracked.

sentences.zh: 誠能本聖學以見之政治，臣見國勢可強，仇恥可雪，兄弟之恩可全，祖宗之制可復，亦何憚而不為此。

translations.literal: If one can truly root government in sage learning, your subject sees that national strength can be restored, enemy shame wiped away, brotherly affection preserved whole, and ancestral institutions recovered—why then hesitate to do this?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly grounds governance in the sage's teaching, I believe national strength can be restored, the humiliation of defeat avenged, fraternal bonds preserved, and ancestral institutions revived—why hesitate to act?

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝優詔答之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor answered with an edict of gracious commendation.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor replied with a gracious edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 三年遷洗馬。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to the post of Palace Steward.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Palace Steward.

sentences.zh: 也先使者乞遣報使，帝堅不許。

translations.literal: Esan's envoy requested that a return envoy be sent; the emperor firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Esen's envoy asked that a return mission be dispatched; the emperor firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 定之疏引故事以請，帝下廷議，竟不果遣。

translations.literal: Dingzhi memorialized citing precedent to request it; the emperor referred it to court deliberation, but in the end no envoy was sent.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhi memorialized citing precedent in support of the request; the emperor referred the matter to court debate, but no envoy was sent in the end.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷右庶子。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to Right Sub-Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to Right Sub-Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 天順改元，調通政司左參議，仍兼侍講。

translations.literal: When the Tianshun reign era began, he was transferred to Left Assistant Director of the Transmission Office, while still concurrently serving as Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianshun era began, he was transferred to Left Assistant Director of the Transmission Office while retaining his post as Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 尋進翰林學士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was advanced to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，進太常少卿，兼侍讀學士，直經筵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended, he was advanced to Vice Minister of Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently serving as Reader-in-Waiting and attending the Classics Lectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Reader-in-Waiting, and lecturer at the Classics Lectures.

sentences.zh: 成化二年十二月，以本官入直文淵閣，進工部右侍郎，兼翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Chenghua, retaining his former office he entered service at the Wenyuan Pavilion, was advanced to Right Vice Minister of Works, and concurrently served as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Chenghua 2, he entered the Wenyuan Pavilion in his existing capacity, was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works, and continued as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 江西、湖廣災，有司方征民賦。

translations.literal: Jiangxi and Huguang suffered disasters, and the local offices were just then levying taxes on the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi and Huguang were stricken by disaster, local officials were still collecting taxes from the people.

sentences.zh: 定之言國儲充積，倉庾至不能容。

translations.literal: Dingzhi said the state's reserves were full to overflowing, and the granaries could scarcely hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhi argued that the state's granaries were overflowing and could scarcely hold any more.

sentences.zh: 而此張口待哺之氓，乃責其租課，非聖主恤下意。

translations.literal: Yet these people who open their mouths awaiting sustenance were still charged rent and levies—this was not the intent of a sage ruler in caring for his subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Yet these starving people were still being taxed—hardly the conduct of a sage ruler who cares for his subjects.

sentences.zh: 帝感其言，即命停征。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved by his words and immediately ordered the levies halted.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his words, the emperor immediately ordered the collections stopped.

sentences.zh: 四年進禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced to Left Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 萬貴妃專寵，皇后希得見，儲嗣未兆。

translations.literal: Consort Wan monopolized favor; the empress seldom gained audience; no heir apparent had yet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wan held the emperor's exclusive favor; the empress was rarely seen; and no heir had yet been designated.

sentences.zh: 郕王女及笄未下嫁。

translations.literal: The daughter of the Prince of Cheng had reached maturity but had not yet been given in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Cheng's daughter had come of age but had not yet been married.

sentences.zh: 定之因久旱，並論及之。

translations.literal: Dingzhi, on the occasion of prolonged drought, discussed these matters together in his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Citing the prolonged drought, Dingzhi raised these matters together in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 且請經筵兼講太祖禦制諸書，斥異端邪教，勿令害政耗財。

translations.literal: He also requested that the Classics Lectures include instruction in the various works composed by the Taizu Emperor, and that heterodox and evil teachings be repudiated, so they would not harm government and waste resources.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the Classics Lectures include the Taizu Emperor's own writings, and that heterodox cults be suppressed before they could corrupt government and drain the treasury.

sentences.zh: 帝留其疏不下。

translations.literal: The emperor kept his memorial and did not release it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor withheld the memorial and took no action on it.

sentences.zh: 五年卒官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，謚文安。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Wen'an, "Cultured and Tranquil."

sentences.zh: 定之謙恭質直，以文學名一時。

translations.literal: Dingzhi was modest, sincere, and straightforward, famed in his time for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhi was modest, plain-spoken, and upright, and was renowned in his day for his literary accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 嘗有中旨命制元宵詩，內使卻立以俟。

translations.literal: Once an inner edict ordered him to compose Lantern Festival poems; a palace eunuch stood aside waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on an imperial command, he was asked to compose Lantern Festival poems while a palace eunuch stood by waiting.

sentences.zh: 據案伸紙，立成七言絕句百首。

translations.literal: He leaned on the desk, spread paper, and on the spot completed a hundred heptasyllabic quatrains.
translations.idiomatic: He spread paper at his desk and instantly produced a hundred seven-character quatrains.

sentences.zh: 又嘗一日草九制，筆不停書。

translations.literal: On another occasion, in a single day he drafted nine imperial edicts, his brush never pausing.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he drafted nine imperial edicts in a single day without pausing.

sentences.zh: 有質宋人名字者，就列其世次，若譜系然，人服其敏博。

translations.literal: When someone questioned him about Song people's names, he would on the spot list their generations as if drawing up a genealogy; people admired his quickness and breadth of learning.
translations.idiomatic: When asked to identify Song dynasty figures by name, he could instantly arrange them by generation as if reading from a family register; all marveled at his quickness and erudition.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：英宗之復辟也，當師旅饑饉之余，民氣未復，權奸內訌，柱石傾移，朝野多故，時事亦孔棘矣。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When Emperor Yingzong restored his rule, it was in the aftermath of armies and famine; the people's spirit had not recovered; powerful villains quarreled within; pillar-stones were overturned; court and countryside had many troubles; affairs of the time were also exceedingly perilous.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, the realm was still reeling from war and famine. Public morale had not recovered, powerful factions were feuding within the court, the pillars of state had been shaken, and affairs at every level were desperately strained.

sentences.zh: 李賢以一身搘拄其間，沛然若有余。

translations.literal: Li Xian, with his single person, propped up affairs in their midst, abundantly as if with strength to spare.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian bore the weight of it almost single-handedly, with strength to spare.

sentences.zh: 獎厲人材，振飭綱紀。

translations.literal: He encouraged talent and restored discipline to the laws and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: He encouraged talent and restored order to the institutions of state.

sentences.zh: 迨憲、孝之世，名臣相望，猶多賢所識拔。

translations.literal: By the reigns of Xian and Xiao, eminent ministers succeeded one another in view, many of them men Xian had recognized and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: By the reigns of the Xian and Xiao emperors, distinguished ministers filled the court—many of them men he had discovered and promoted.

sentences.zh: 偉哉宰相才也。

translations.literal: Grand indeed was his talent as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: What grand ministerial talent he possessed.

sentences.zh: 彭時、商輅侃侃守義，盡忠獻納，粹然一出於正。

translations.literal: Peng Shi and Shang Lu, upright and steadfast in righteousness, devoted their loyalty and offered remonstrance, pure and wholly arising from rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shi and Shang Lu spoke with principled forthrightness, serving with loyal devotion and offering candid counsel—all of it grounded in rectitude.

sentences.zh: 其於慈懿典禮，非所謂善成君德者歟？

translations.literal: In the rites concerning Empress Dowager Ci, were they not what is called those who well completed their ruler's virtue?
translations.idiomatic: In the rites honoring Empress Dowager Ci, did they not exemplify what it means to help complete a ruler's moral cultivation?

sentences.zh: 輅科名與宋王曾、宋庠埒，德望亦無愧焉。

translations.literal: Lu's examination rank was on a par with Song Wang Ceng and Song Bao, and in moral stature he had nothing to be ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Lu's examination rank matched those of Song Wang Ceng and Song Bao, and his moral standing was equally beyond reproach.

sentences.zh: 呂原、嶽正、劉定之雖相業未優，而原之行誼，正之氣概，定之之建白，鹹有可稱，故以時次，並列於篇。

translations.literal: Although Lu Yuan, Yue Zheng, and Liu Dingzhi did not excel as chief ministers, Yuan's conduct and integrity, Zheng's spirit and bearing, and Dingzhi's memorial proposals all had points worth praise; therefore, by chronological order, they are listed together in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuan, Yue Zheng, and Liu Dingzhi did not rank among the greatest ministers, yet Yuan's integrity, Zheng's force of character, and Dingzhi's memorial counsel all merit mention; they are therefore included here in chronological order.
